title: Buggy Apple Watch Version
body:
I like the app, but the Apple Watch version is so buggy I seriously doubt it is even tested.

The syncing is unreliable, and it usually takes a while for completions logged in the watch to register on the phone. Whenever a task is completed on the watch, it will more often than not show it as not completed for a while, and only sometimes is this solved without requiring to manually complete the task once more. The worst offender in my opinion are the timers. The seconds marker moves way too fast most of the time for some reason. After pausing and unpausing, it will start the timer from zero. Again, this is sometimes only a visual bug but at other times progress is somehow lost and the app loses track of how much time had already passed. These are only some of the bugs I’ve noticed.

I’ve been using the app for well over a year now and I feel compelled to write this review because in that time none of the bugs I’ve encountered were fixed. On the contrary, the Apple Watch version seems to get progressively buggier with each update. I just wish the Apple Watch version had the same quality as the iPhone version, which is excellent and the reason I got the app in the first place.

title: Excellent app
body:
Love this app! It offers lots of customisability and integrates with Apple devices really well. Well worth the money. 

Some features I would suggest: 
- The star icon on the bottom right leads you to a statistics screen. These stats are great, but I personally would also love to see a heatmap of the whole year for my tasks. The app already lets you see a monthly heatmap for your tasks (e.g. an overview of what days you completed/skipped in December), but I’d love to also see a yearly version of this on the statistics screen. 
- There is feature where you can share your stats in a PNG image, which includes the app icon. This is very trivial, but this app icon doesn’t update if the user has set a custom icon for the app. If you could make the icon in this image match whatever the user has set, that would make it consistent.

title: A year on streaks
body:
This week marks a year on Streaks. I’m not addicted, I’m committed.  Streaks has helped me focus my intentions into completions.

I would consider myself a creative, active person but somewhat scattered in my approach to personal growth. It’s very easy to let “other’’ things get in the way of what you want to do.

I used to draw most days, which is a lot. NOW I draw everyday. In manageable and achievable goals. My level of drawing has jumped another level because of my commitment to grow. Streaks has most certainly done that.  

This year I have drawn on 1300 plus occasions, practised piano five times a week, written a screen play, a graphic novel and a stage play.  

Streaks has allowed me to focus on what I love to do. It is the most powerful tool I use.

Thank you Streaks team.

The once off purchase is also amazing, so many apps hit you with expensive subscriptions. I would recommend this to anyone trying to get a better hold over their life and accomplish the important things that matter to them. I also love that it’s customisable. Now I don’t have to think about all the things I need to do. I just open up streaks throughout the day and it has it all there for me. Great option for managing ADHD. I never write reviews but I had to for this because it’s so good.

body:

Improvement can be implemented as follows: 1. Streaks to be segregated into subfolders (eg. Exercise -> type of exercise category such as cardiovascular, resistance, etc, and then within those subfolders the relevant exercise program). 2. The Tasks being listed not by chronological creation but by their alpha-numeric order. - Note that you can reorder (Sort Tasks) by “Tap settings” -> “Long press and drag”.

 Tasks. 3. When creating a Task, the creation of an additional Task by default saves the newly created Task to that of the previous Tasks location. If that Task is to be the start of a new dataset, the user can then specify the relevant Task for which it is to be saved and the process continues accordingly. - I will add to this review if I utilise the app more rather than migrating to another one and if there is other functionality that I believe needs implementing for the app to be fit-for-purpose.

title: Always useful
body:
There are so many ways to make use of this app! I love that I can set so many different kinds of goals and how I can track my progress! - From exercise routines to skill practice, to prioritising time for myself or time spent working with my kids HW or skill development. I can track application to chores or supporting health. 
I can choose time lengths to discipline myself to a task, or multiple counts of a task per day/week/month etc.
I can adjust how many times per day in how many days per week. I can choose which days in a week I specifically want to complete a task. 
It pings you with positive encouragement for achieving goals, you can choose from a vast variety of colour combinations to personalise it (including allowing the background to change at random or using light/dark mode) and you can archive goals you made, but don’t want to delete them (insteadsuspend them for a time).

I even love the different symbols you can choose from to match each of your tasks - making it easier to find the one you want to check off.
Also, best addition I found is when it started syncing to my Apple Watch! *I can check off items without even opening my phone.

If you like checklists, setting or tracking history of any goals or find you are really busy— this app will make life easier. (The calendar in the app even allows you to open it and fix any errors you entered or if you forgot to check off a previous day.)

*I just recommend taking the time to explore its options and try a couple of ways to count your goals. (Sometimes I found that one way of using the app was not as helpful as another, but I can always edit it.)

body:

I asked for assistance and the team who said they have no idea why it happens but said it’s a bug that fixes itself in two days.. 2 days+ pass and yet to see any improvement. They also said they are working on this in a new patch? 

I’m sorry, but if you are paying $7.99 (highly priced as compared to other organisation apps) and it only allows 12 recurring actions, you would expect in the very least that it works. It is a fault not a simple bug. 

It’s sad I can’t get a refund for this. I was hoping it would help with my depression, reminding me to have a shower, brush my teeth, brush my hair and do basic task. Really it’s only made me more stressed from it’s lack of functionality. My recommendation, don’t waste your money.

title: Feeling accountable
body:
Have been using the app for a week now and it seems to balance all the right elements to reward you when keeping a streak, whilst keeping you accountable for the habits you wish to keep. An important feature, which I didn’t realize until using the app, was the ability to keep a record of your habits over time and gauge when you are least likely to perform a habit (e.g. late in the week); with this information you can mentally prepare for that time in the future and have a greater chance of following through with the habit. 

It’s looks great, works exactly as it should and negative habits are a wonderful feature. The only two things I would change is an optional ‘advance’ setting providing more in-depth graphical information, however, I am not even sure If I would ever use it. Also, would be nice if a habit (based on certain criteria) would ‘talk’ to you (with a speech bubble or something) and spur you on to rebuild a large habit streak, since if you break a big streak one could benefit from some encouragement. Would love to see this feature!

title: A seriously motivating app
body:
If you’re someone who likes to keep a Snapchat streak going and who wants to better their life, this app is for you!! 

Seriously, it is worth the money. I can’t afford to splash money on just anything so I didn’t buy this app right away. But I soon just thought what the hell and bought it anyway, and I’m so glad that I did. It’s really such a simple concept, you just add the tasks that you want to do, the app reminds you to do it or else you lose your streak. I’ve read some people on here just calling it a To Do list and that it’s not worth the money, but I’ve always wanted to journal but have quit just a few days after starting. But for the past 3 weeks that I’ve had this app I have journaled everyday. Just a regular To Do list app wouldn’t motivate me to journal daily, but this one does for fear of losing the streak I’ve worked hard to maintain. Other things I’ve been making sure I complete everyday include taking my vitamins, eating at least one fruit or vegetable, reading for 10 minutes, taking my dog for a walk - all of which I struggle to do regularly, let alone consecutively everyday for almost a month. 

So don’t worry about the money and just get the app, you’ll thank yourself when you’ve got all these good habits and you feel like you’re getting your life on track.

The Apple Watch companion app is a must have if you've got it. 5 stars both.

title: Nice balance between simplicity and utility
body:
I've tried both Streaks and its nearest competitor Productive, and Streaks manages to be easier to actually maintain. Productive is feature-packed, which means you tend to overload it with too many habits that you quickly fall behind on.

By contrast, Streaks has no time-of-day habits, and limits you to six habits total. This is definitely a selling point, since it forces you to think about what's actually important to you rather than trying to hold yourself to an impossible standard.

Streaks also has some nice HealthKit-powered smarts built in: reducing the busy-work of habits by automatically logging where possible certainly helps with actually maintaining a habit of using the app.

It's also the second app I use with an actually useful Apple Watch complication!

title: O melhor
body:
Já testei todo tipo de app de hábitos,esse eu sempre via mas não queria por ser pago,mas resolvi testar e valeu a pena.Foram os 25,00 mais bem pagos. O melhor é que não tem assinatura,você só paga uma vez e depois o app é seu.
Pontos positivos:
-Design(o app mais lindo que já vi).
-Recompensa(quando você cumpre todos os hábitos da página,os ícones ficam dourados e é bem bonito).
-Usabilidade (muito simples de usar e tem tutoriais)
-Estatísticas (hábitos separados e hábitos juntos,tem histórico geral)
-Personalização(muitos ícones,cores e sons).
-Botão de ação (permite abrir outros apps direto dele,se você colocar ler a Bíblia,pode configurar e ele abre o app)
-Sincronização perfeita
-Coleta dados do app Saúde(e é o melhor fazendo isso,já testei outros e nenhum foi tão bom)se quiser ter hábitos de calorias perdidas ou tantos passos,esse app é o certo.
Pontos Para Melhorar:
-Mais hábitos(Só tem 24,o que é pouco se você quiser concentrar toda a sua rotina nele).
-Subtarefas(como o app tem hábitos limitados,temos que agrupar em um só várias coisas,seria legal ter subtarefas em cada hábito para ir ticando quando fosse completadas,exemplo,uso vários apps de treinamento cerebral,e ao invés de colocar cada app,coloquei apenas o hábito de treinar a mente,com 7 vezes ao dia,mas como não tem subtarefas,eu fica perdida sem saber quais apps já usei,ou o hábito de dona de casa,onde englobo todas as tarefas domesticas,mas de novo,não tenho como saber quais foram feitas,isso faz precisar de um app externo o que não me agradou).
-Tons pasteis (Tem muitas cores para os ícones dos hábitos mas não tem tantas para as páginas,as cores que tem são bem gritantes,com excessão de algumas).
-Sistema de ranking e levels(seria legal poder competir com outros usuários e ver as classificações,isso seria motivador e até hoje não achei um app que faça isso além do flynow).
-Poderia ter medalhas e troféus conforme você fosse progredindo e cumprindo seus hábitos,isso iria motivar e aumentar a disciplina.
-Possibilidade de criar um perfil e interagir com outros usuários,para cumprir metas juntos e etc.
-Metas(não sei porque os desenvolvedores ainda não entenderam que hábitos e metas andam de mãos dadas,por exemplo,eu crio o hábito de ler,mas não posso criar a meta de 50 livros no ano).

author: O. Oshikanlu

title: iCloud sync is terrible
body: I stopped using this app across multiple devices (just iPhone) years ago, because the sync over iCloud was complete garbage. Tried setting it up again today across devices to see if anything had improved—it’s atrocious. I purged everything from iCloud (four Streaks entries appeared there). Upon re-enabling it, I got deleted items, duplicated items, items out of sync, and it even broke the iPhone app where it now fails to even let me complete an item (rolling back the completion). It’s utterly useless. To be clear, this is not the developer’s fault—iCloud sync is deplorable on every app where it’s used, including Apple’s own apps. But the developer should consider using something else. It’s a shame, because the underlying simple idea behind this app is good. If you’re going to use it, stick to just one device.
author: Mickers

title: This app is great
body:
I really enjoy using this app to develop habits! It’s almost just right for me. The app is easy to navigate, and it’s satisfying to create a new habit and click the buttons. The introduction of the Halloween theme was definitely a nice touch. Makes me feel like the app gets and respects its viewers. No one has to make a Halloween theme but you did it anyway and I feel special when changes like that occur. 

The only thing I’d suggest is that sometimes I’d like to give my habits a specific name, but the space is a bit limited—only 28 characters. This makes it a bit harder to set an intention. There’s a section where you can write notes, but it’s just not the same as seeing the text on the screen right away when you open the app. 

All in all I’m happy with the app. Definitely worth the money.

title: Fantastic app!
body: I almost never write reviews, but a couple days into using this one and I had to share in case anyone was doubting this purchase. I’ve been using another tally app for a long time now and was always annoyed that the only way to get full functionality was to do a yearly subscription. That’s ridiculous! I also really wanted to use Siri to log calories and water and so on. I downloaded some free tally apps and free trials, but they all had something I didn’t like about them. Anyways, Streaks is perfect! I have Siri Shortcuts set up for my Health app that tie into this app so I can tell my data to Siri and she updates both apps. I prefer using Streaks for checking my progress on habits just because it’s a much cleaner, visual app than health. There is also so much customization available with Streaks - I’m really happy I bought it!

title: Never write app reviews
body:
Have tried 3 other habit apps and have been disappointed with complicated / busy displays, unintuitive etc. Wanted simple nice tactile UI which is easy / simple to use and flexible. 

8 days in it has already made a huge difference for me personally. I didn’t think I would possibly need more than 24 slots - but based on how well things are going I can see why others have raised this. 100pct worth the 8 dollars.

One thing worth noting from a UI perspective - short taps and long holds unlock different things. At first it was unintuitive for me to do a long hold on a button but its really smart and reduces clutter - other app devs should consider.

title: Great, but it’s missing something.
body:

And example of this is, let’s say you have “brush your teeth” as a Streak and you want it to require 2 completions (brushing in the morning and in the evening). Well, if you complete just one of those, it doesn’t count for anything and will not show up in the overall graph. Let’s say you went awhile only brushing your teeth in the morning, well, that’s as good as not doing it at all because it doesn’t “track” partial completions.

There’s got to be a way to integrate this into the app, it’s a good way to visualize when you are doing well vs. doing ok vs. doing poorly.

Otherwise, the app is easy on the eyes, but the widgets are pretty ugly, I don’t know how to tackle that one hah!

title: Good, but needs to be better
body:
This app has a lot more potential, particularly for breaking bad habits.

I do not think I could stop touching my face entirely cold turkey, but the only info I can record is that I failed to completely abstain. It would be helpful if I could count the number of times I touched my face by holding down the habit icon. Then I could track gradual improvements over time.

The most success I have had is with a daily push-up habit. But again I can’t record if I do a second set. Similarly, if I back off a bit one day and only do a set of 40 reps instead of 50, I ought to count the streak broken. However, doing a partial set could be a big win some days, and it would be nice if I could enter reps on the habit icon after pushing it.

So, please allow multiple counts of habits, and please allow a custom complication for some habits prompting a rep count or duration.

Developer offers friendly support when issues are encountered and keeps his software up to the latest standards. 
Congratulations on a job well done!
author: AC@Faubourgs

title: Great app! Use it for my physio exercices.
body:
I use it to remind myself of every physio exercise that i have to do every day. It wirks well, simple, motivating, no complaints. Highly recommend to people around me.

@ the developers, here’s a few things that i would like you to add/change : 
-icons: more simple positions, so that they correspond to physio exercises better. Take a person standing, then put their arms in various positions; then do the same with someone sitting, pushing against a wall; you can look some up, i think I’m probably not the only one who uses it for that!
-icons turning gold: honestly, that’s the most motivating part for me, not so much the streaks. Can you make it so that if you only have 2, 3, 4 icons on there (rest is empty), that it still turns gold when you’ve finished them? Currently it only turns gold if you have 6/6, but not 5/5, 4/4, etc.
-icons: physio exercises look alike, so it would be cool if we could color-code the individual icons for easier recognition 
-make it so that when you’re interrupted doing a timed task, you can save your progress to catch up later
author: Cloelieroy

title: Works for me
body: I set two new years resolutions for myself this year.  Coding something every day and giving up drinking pop, cold turkey.  I’ve attempted both of these in the past and was never able to stick with it.  Turns out my addiction to drinking pop was less consuming than my addiction to watching the stupid little number tick up everyday.  Both habits are at 55 days and I’m looking to add another to my daily routine.  These apps have never worked for me in the past, but for some reason this time it just clicked.
author: Ayonunum

title: Change your habits, change your life.
body: This is a great app to help you with changing your daily habits. While you can only have 12 habits tracked at one time, it offers great flexibility in the way that they look, and when you can get reminders for completion. It's simplistic design removes the flood that you don't need allowing you to focus on getting things done. It also has a companion Apple Watch complication to make logging your completions in a seamless easy manner. One of my favourite things about this app is you can change the colour of your icon for your screen. If you are OCD this makes your life. The only thing I would change is allowing you to drop habits and archive them to use again later.
author: Urban Native Girl

title: Life is just a game

Simple perfect app at a great price (except to those weirdos who think all software should be free).
Only thing: would be nice to have more than 12 items. Not all habits are daily. But this is a minor quibble. Clearly a lot of thought went into the design. An hour after you have set it up you will feel like you been using it forever. 
Truly impressive.

title: Good design, weird to use
body:
It’s a beautifully designed app, love the colours the sounds and the amount of customization you can do.

The weird part is in the organization, you get a maximum of 12 habits, no more, which is okay because that’s a lot, but they’re split into two groups of 6, and you can only make changes to one of those groups at a time, not all the habits.

The app doesn’t give you any information on how many habits you completed on a given day, or a history of all your habits so that you can see your progress over time... it only gives you stats on each habit, and for some reason on the groups of 6 habits that you have (again, weird). It gives you graphs and pie charts and all that, but not a simple “this is how many out of 12 you completed each day” to see your improvement over time.

Most of the App don't give you this option and your habit is due since 00.01. After spending so much money on different Apps, I eventually find this App and I’m so happy with it.

author: Jktw98

title: Best Habit Tracker Hands Down.
body:
Everything it needs to be. No features locked behind paywalls or ridiculous subscriptions. Interface is simple and extremely vibrant and customizable. I was happily surprised by how many pre generated habits they had set up and the hundreds of icons to choose from when creating your own goals. Track habits in pretty much every way. Simple to use once you’ve set up all personal features. Statistics for each goal are simple but still in depth. Satisfying  checking off completed goals. Never bombarded with reminders but are helpful when needed. Lastly, and probably the best feature, the lock screen/home widget is super convenient to see at glance all daily habits and check them off as completed without opening the app. 
For the price of a cup of coffee this is a must for productivity in my opinion and the best habit tracker currently in the App Store. Extremely pleased with this app👍

title: Has promise, but...
body:

E.g. it will give me reminders or show activities as incomplete that are not supposed to happen today. 

Also the results summary needs a redesign (graph axes are unlabelled, they use a line graph where it should be a bar graph, basic data visualization stuff like that). 

There is a button that seems to flip my card over and show other activities in a different colour. What is this? What is it for? The tutorial doesn’t say. 

Is there a way to give feedback other than in a review? I haven’t found it.

A promising app that needs some improvements.

title: Great app. Could use some improvement.
body:
This app is definitely the best and most functional habit tracker I've used. 

I feel like there are a few things that could be added and improved upon. A big one for me is the fact that the app badge shows that there is a task that needs completing but when you open the app it doesn't say which task you need to do at that time. I've set specific times for me to do certain things and when I have more that one thing outstanding and only wish to do the one I need to at that particular time, it gets confusing. I wish there was a badge in the app on the specific task that needs to be completed at that time. At this point I can only guess which task I need to complete to get the app badge to go away. Other than that it's a great app. 

I also think it would be a great idea to carry over a few features from the "Productive" app. That app was my main before this but I feel Streaks has much more functionality and potential.

Keep it up.

title: I use this app every day!
body: There aren't many apps I can say I use and interact with every day, but this is one of the few. This app is a great motivator and has helped me to achieve daily tasks that are important to me. My music, writing, second language acquisition and fitness have all improved in leaps and bounds as a direct result of Streaks. In a way, this app acts as kind of a World of Warcraft "daily quest" that taps into that same compulsive drive I feel while gaming and farming for trophies and achievements. I would love to see trophies, titles and badges or some other kind of recognition type of reward incorporated into this app in the future, to motivate me to reach certain milestone streaks (ie: 25 day streaks, 50, 100, 250, 500, etc). This is by far the most consulted, the most used and the most helpful app on my iPhone.

author: gabhert

title: Hochgelobt und bescheiden motivierend
body:
„Wenn Du es heute nicht schaffst, wird dein Streak beendet“ ist die Standard-Meldung dieses Programms. („…und die Mama gibt dir keinen Keks…“ fehlt irgendwie noch). Pädagogik aus dem frühen 20. Jahrhundert, bäh.
Liebe Programmierer, bitte lest mal ein Buch über Motivationstraining, Coaching etc., vornehmlich eines, das nach 1980 erschienen ist. Dieses „wenn du nicht, dann böse Konsequenzen“ ist einfach zu schlecht und zu veraltet für eine App, die gleichzeitig so (schön)einfach gestrickt ist aber für 5 Fr. verkauft wird. Und die so viel Potential hätte!
Wie wäre beispielsweise eine Liste von Benefits, die sich der Kunde beim Erstellen einer Aufgabe selbst zusammenstellen kann, und an die die App ihn dann erinnert? Oder einfach ein paar positive Motivationen als Standardtexte? 
Das wäre innovativer und motivierender. Und dann gibt’s auch 5 Sterne für die ansonsten sehr gute App

title: Almost perfect
body:
This app is really great and impressive. However, there are some serious shortcomings. Apart from some annoying bugs (history not resetting and reappearing, previously removed tasks showing up etc.), the main downside is that the app imposes an artificial limit of 24 habits only. 

If you consider the fact that the user can also add negative habits, it becomes clear that it is perfectly reasonable to require an unlimited number of habits. Or, at least, 50-60 because one can also add weekly, fortnightly, or specific days habits. Other apps offer unlimited habits and I’m considering switching to those. Which is a shame because this app has a lot of potential. I really can’t understand why they impose this limit… 

It would really make a difference if the developers introduced unlimited habits.

body:
以往的习惯软件往往需要“打开手机→点开图标”这个门槛，但steaks搭配watch完美避免了这个缺点：用watch记录可以避免手机的信息轰炸，更专注于工作本身。方便自己在养成习惯的同时，也养成记录习惯的习惯。
这种形式一开始会难以上手，所以不需要期望一次弄完美，只要多调试就会越来越好用！
唯一美中不足的是，番茄钟功能还不完善，并不是通常意义上的连续计时/休息，希望改进。

title: 希望可以加入记事功能。
body:
每天完成一个习惯时，多少会有一些思考、感悟以及对今天完成情况的评价，发现这个软件并没有这个功能。
我认为加入这样一个总结功能是很有必要的。没有反思就没有进步，对今天的习惯完成情况作出总结，会更有助于习惯的培养。

关于记事本的呈现形式，希望可以按时间流的形式集中呈现，这样更加方便对自己的心路历程作出总结。

title: 不要有番茄钟功能！

title: Besser als andere
body: Ich habe bewusst zu Streaks gewechselt. Ich wollte eine App, mit der ich Habits bilden kann, die ich nur unter der Woche mache, nicht am Wochenende. Das können nicht alle Apps. Leider gibt es hier dafür keinen Urlaubsmodus. Ich kann meine Streaks daher nicht im Urlaub pausieren. Auch Feiertage können nicht berücksichtigt werden. Das könnte man verbessern. Die Menüführung ist gewöhnungsbedürftig. Aber wenn man drin ist, ist das Konzept und die Gestaltung recht nurtzerfreundlich. Ich habe mir Kategorien angelegt. Es gibt eine Ansicht, in der ich alle Habits einer Kategorie sehe. Das kann man so einstellen, dass man nur sieht, was zum Beispiel von der Morgenroutine noch offen ist. Das ist hilfreich. Leider kann ich in der Übersicht die Reihenfolge der Kategorien nicht ändern. Meine Übersicht fängt jetzt mit der Abend- und dann mit der Morgenroutine, statt in der richtigen Reihenfolge: Morgen-, Schreibtisch-, Nachmittag- und Abendroutine. Das wäre praktisch, wenn ich in der Übersicht die Reihenfolge ändern könnte. Aber das sind Details. Insgesamt ist die App gut gemacht und sehr hilfreich. Es ist die App, die ich am Häufigsten benutze. (Seid ich Instagram und anderen Quatsch gelöscht habe).

title: Gute App — mit gravierenden Bugs
body: TLdr: Super Gewohnheitstracker mit gravierenden Problemen mit Widgets, Apple Watch App und bei der Synchronisation via iCloud. Daher lieber nur lokal, auf einem Gerät nutzen. PROBLEME 1. Widgets aktualisieren nicht oder zeigen sogar garnichts an 2. Duplikate von Gewohnheiten entstehen 3. Verlauf verschwindet 4 bestehende Gewohnheiten verschwinden; werden von der App gelöscht… LÖSUNGSANSÄTZE A) Bei Aktivierung der Synchronisation via iCloud entstehen Duplikate. Zwar gibt es in der App eine Funktion, um Duplikate zu finden und zu löschen – aber kurze Zeit später tritt das Problem erneut auf, daher keine Lösung. B) Backup und Löschen hilft nicht. Innerhalb der App lässt sich ein Backup der Daten manuell anstoßen – doch selbst nach Löschen aller Daten und anschließendem Import des Backups treten die gleichen Probleme wieder auf… C) Deaktivieren der Synchronisation, Löschen der App, anschließende Neu-Installation, Import des Backups – es treten die gleichen Probleme erneut auf… ERFOLGREICHE LÖSUNG - App löschen - neuen Account einrichten - alle Gewohnheiten manuell neu einrichten RESULTAT & FOLGE - Fortschritt verloren - Immenser Zeitaufwand - Frustration & Entmutigung FAZIT - Sync nicht aktivieren! - Streaks nur auf einem Gerät nutzen: iPhone

title: Super durchdachte App. Danke!
body: Hallo zusammen, ich habe mir heute das Package mit Streaks und Workout gekauft und bin sehr glücklich darüber! Die Apps sind super. Vor allem, dass man an den richtigen Stellen detaillierte Einstellmöglichkeiten hat. Da war ich schon oft an einer Stelle wo och befürchtet habe, dass funktioniert jetzt so nicht, wie ich das will, und doch, es geht!! Danke dafür! Fünf Dinge, sind mir dann doch aufgefallen, die noch eine super Ergänzung wären: 1.: ich würde gerne erledigte Aufgaben weiter tracken können. Also z.B. wenn mein Ziel ist, 2L Wasser am Tag zu trinken und ich heute aber 3L trinke, würde ich das auch gerne vermerken können, obwohl die Aufgabe natürlich bei 2L schon als erledigt markiert ist. Gleiches auch für wöchentliche und monatliche Aufgaben. Das Ganze sollte dann auch in der Statistik zu sehen sein. (Dies gilt auch für die Workout App - also nicht nur z.B. 3 von 5 Tagen, sondern auch z.B. 9 Workouts diese Woche) 2.: Wäre eventuell auch ein jährliches Ziel möglich? 3.: Könnte man das Einbeziehen in die Anzeige für den Kennzeichenzähler nicht nur auf Uhrzeit, sondern auch auf Tage und Uhrzeit begrenzen? 4.: Wenn man eine „tägliche“ Aufgabe hat, wie z.B. 5 Tage die Woche, oder immer Dienstag und Donnerstag, wärs super, wenn man auf dem Aufgabenpunkt sehen kann, wieviel vom wöchentlichen Ziel man schon erreicht hat, nicht nur wenn man in die Statistik wechselt (die ist ja dann ausführlicher mit Serie/Bestes/Diese Woche/30 Tage). 5.: beim nachträglich eintragen wärs toll, wenn man auch die Uhrzeit anpassen könnte (am besten auch gesammelt für mehrere Erledigungen) - hab meine Eintragungen aus einer anderen App gestern zu Streaks übertragen und jetzt ist natürlich überall gestern Abend als Uhrzeit hinterlegt (jetzt muss ich quasi Tagelang alle Eintragung zur entsprechenden Uhrzeit wiederholen) Das wären echt noch super Erweiterungen und würden mein Erlebnis perfekt machen! Ansonsten ist das echt ein 5*Produkt, und ich bin echt froh, mich dazu entschlossen zu haben!

title: Badges
body:
Ich bin sehr zufrieden mit der App! 

Neben der bereits ausführlichen Statistik, würde ich es toll finden, wenn es eine Art Badges/Medaillen als zusätzliche Belohnung geben würde. Beispielsweise für Streaks bei einzelnen Aufgaben, bei Erfüllung über einen längeren Zeitraum, usw...

title: Keep it simple!
body: I love your product and its unique, bold design. Please keep it simple, it got a little cluttered recently. The filter at the top seems odd to me. Do users have so many tasks, and if so, does it need to have a prominent placement like that? — Also, using an arrow icon is probably not the best choice for a filter. I understand this represents the overview of all tasks, but I’d choose an icon that helps understand the feature faster. The UX is very unique already, meaning it takes more time to get used to it compared to other apps.

title: Awesome!
body:
Best habit app I've come across so far. Really love the design, it's clean but also flexible enough. 

It syncs with my Apple Watch, has a MacOS App and much more.

Really happy with it, as a developer myself I can see how much effort went into this application.

body:

Nutz es zur Zeit z.B. für die Welpen Erziehung- da du Timer / Erinnerungen u.s.w. erstellen kannst in einer ToDo. Vorher hab ich es für mich privat (Sport etc.) genutzt. Also je Lebenssituationen immer anpassbar 

Hab die schon 2 Jahre lang und nutz sie auch immer auf der Appel Watch.

title: Eigentlich tolle App, aber Sync ist eine Katastrophe
body: Ich benutze die App täglich und bin grundsätzlich total begeistert, weil ich damit auch an ungeliebten Aufgaben dran bleibe. Aber seitdem der Sync komplett auf iCloud umgestellt wurde, führt die App ein Eigenleben. Abgesehen davon, dass der Sync (Watch, iPhone, iPad etc) ewig dauert oder ein vollständiges Beenden der App erfordert, auch die Widgets zeigen unterschiedliche Sachen an. Am katastrophalsten ist aber, dass neue Aufgaben ohne Ankündigung gelöscht werden und alte Aufgaben wie Zombies wieder auftauchen. Schönen Dank, dass meine Aufgabenhistorie für sechs Aufgaben einfach gleich mit gelöscht wurde!!! Ich habe die Apps mittlerweile auf allen zusätzlichen Geräten gelöscht, weil der iCloud-Sync mit den Zeitstempeln überhaupt nicht klarkommt. So schade um die App, die mal wirklich gut funktioniert hat.

body:

title: Sehr gut aber verbesserungsfähig
body: Großartige App um diszipliniert Aufgaben zu erfüllen. Dennoch hätte ich einige Verbesserungsvorschläge. - Mehr Seiten und Aufgaben - Seite einen Namen geben oder eine Kategorie - Es wäre es gut wenn man sich eine Seite anlegen könnte mit Aufgaben die man nur einmal erfüllen möchte und die dann wieder verschwinden (To-Do Liste) - Außerdem wäre es gut wenn man Aufgaben miteinander verknüpfen könnte ( Beispiel: Immer wenn ich Beine oder Arme trainiere möchte ich auch Dehnen) sonst muss man diese Aufgabe nämlich extra mehrmals anlegen - Außerdem wäre es gut wenn die Einstellungen für die Wiederholung vielfältiger wären und man beispielsweise ,Erster Tag des Monats oder letzter Tag des Monats, auswählen könnte und die Wiederholdauer selbst bestimmbar ist und nicht auf 30 Tage begrenzt. Eventuell könnte man auch ein festes Datum für die Aufgabe festlegen, z.B immer am 10 Tag des Monats

body: Ich liebe diese App, aber bei mir überschreibt das Handy immer die Watch App, das nervt richtig. Ich benutze für die Eingabe meist meine Uhr, aber wenn ich die Handy App mal einen Tag nicht aufmache, dann synchronisieren die Streaks nicht richtig und ich muss die Ergebnisse vom Vortag (die ich in der Uhr eingegeben habe) manuell im Handykalender nachtragen, weil die im Handy fehlenden Daten die vorhandenen Daten auf der Uhr überschreiben. Dieser Extraschritt nervt mich total, wozu habe ich denn eine App auf der Uhr? Ich hatte Streaks ursprünglich für die synchronisierte Nutzung auf beiden Geräten ausgesucht, vielleicht könnte dieser Fehler beim nächsten Update behoben werden?
author: Charlychamaeleon

title: Love it! Also suggestions:
body:
- add the ability to overcharge a task!
(Say I want to do do at least 3 learning sessions a day, but happened to do 4. There seams to be no way to add the 4. session to the statistics.)
- there is this concept that to train a habit you should always try to do at least an painfully easy version of what you want to accomplish (like: goal = read a chapter -> easy version = read a page, or maybe only one sentence) to Programm it into your system; maybe even do a little bit more towards the goal. 
So please add the ability to create multistep task where you can set how many steps have to be completed before it’s counts.
Or maybe just an easy mode (with Titel) you can add to a task and complete for have a star.
author: Riu_Wystn

title: Not enough task slots / pages for grouping tasks
body:
Great app, great interface. Easy, minimalist design, yet all functionality I wish for my habit tracking. Tasks are organised in pages, with maximum 6 pages per task and maximum 4 pages in total. This is very good as it allows to organise tasks for different day time / categories.

But one (big) negative point: 
It doesn’t offer enough pages to group tasks. 
I think, 6 pages would be perfect for me. 

Here is why: 
I am currently organising my morning routine, my daily work goals, my sports/reading goals and my unwinding/mindfulness goals with this app. In principle this works fine, and not all of them need the 6 goals per page, but some others would need more, which makes me having to mix tasks of different categories on one page. So, I am missing space to organise my tasks into groups that make more sense. Also, I would like to separate weekly tasks (ie ready 2 scientific papers per week) on a separate page. 

Therefore, 2 more pages would be perfect. Not necessarily in order to have 36 tasks in total, that’s quite a lot. But in order to group the tasks with more sense, that would be nice. 

If then one could also add a title to each page, it would be even better and definitely worth 5 stars :)

so fehlen mir z. B. Symbole für Jonglieren, Kettle-Bell, Handstand usw.

title: Schlicht, Übersichtlich und super hilfreich
body:
Das schlichte Layout sorgt für eine super Übersicht.
Die Bedienung ist sehr einfach. Änderungen (z.B. eine Aufgabe an einem anderen Tag als erledigt markieren) sind schnell gemacht.

Die Statistiken sind super (Jahres-, Monatsübersicht mit Angaben zu welcher Zeit welche Aktivitäten durchgeführt wurden). Sehr informativ und verständlich.

Hinzu kommen gut funktionierende Siri-Befehle (sollte ein Befehl nicht funktionieren dann den Befehl in „Kurzbefehle“ öffnen und dort den blauen „Link“ für die Aktivität antippen und neu auswählen; dann geht der Kurzbefehl und auch per Sprache).

Alles in allem eine sehr gute App für seine regelmäßigen Aufgaben. Perfekt für die Selbstkontrolle und Motivation. Sie ist das Geld wert!

title: Unendlicher Wert
body:
Diese App hat mein Leben verändert. Wenn man sich der Macht von Gewohnheiten bewusst ist, dann ist diese App einfach ein Sprungbrett zum Erfolg Reichtum und Wohlstand . Ganz nach dem Motto: „Der stete Tropfen hüllt den Stein“ setzten man sich ein Ziel welches man erreichen will und bricht es anschließend soweit herunter, dass man dafür jeden Tag wirklich nur eine Kleinigkeit tun muss. Für diese tägliche Kleinigkeit (Bsp: täglich 15 min. eine Sprache lernen; ein paar Liegestützen machen; paar Minuten Dehnübungen etc.) braucht es kaum Überwindung, jedoch sind die Ergebnisse am Jahresende enorm!! 
Durch diesen minimalen Zeiteinsatz pro Tag kann ich mittlerweile fast eine neue Sprache verstehen und sprechen, bin viel dehnbarer geworden und schaffe es fast Plach-Liegestützen zu machen. 

Kleiner Tipp für unerfahrene Nutzer: Beim Routinen etablieren lieber erst mal nur eine oder zwei in den Alltag integrieren. Erst dann weitere hinzufügen, wenn die vorherigen zur GEWOHNHEIT geworden sind und keine Disziplin mehr zum umsetzten erfordern, sondern automatisiert ablaufen.

Diese App ist bei richtiger Anwendung hunderte Euro Wert.
author: Tom😄

ABER: Für mich reicht die Anzahl der Aufgaben mit einer Begrenzung von 12 einfach nicht aus! Wird das verändert und der Rest so gelassen wie’s ist dann ist die App wirklich vollumfänglich perfekt!

title: Absturz auf Apple Watch
body:
Seit watchOS 7 läuft die App nicht mehr auf der Apple Watch Series 3. Die Watch wurde neu gestartet und die App auch neu installiert. 

Eine kurze Ladesequenz ist zu sehen, danach  wird die App beendet. 

Vorher lief die App sehr stabil und ich war sehr zufrieden damit. Die App ist auf jeden Fall 5 Sterne wert. Nutze sie nun nur am iPhone, bis der Fehler behoben ist.

Edit: läuft wieder. Danke, für die schnelle Behebung.

title: App is ok but has several issues
body: I like the app, but the UI is really weird and takes some time to get used to it. What really bugs me is that there are completely unnecessary restrictions. Why don’t you allow users to enter their goals as decimal numbers? It’s super annoying for example that I’m only able to define  my fitness goals in integers from a predefined list. I can set a goal of 2 or 3 km a day, but not 2.5. that’s annoying. Also 5 flights of stairs as the minimum per day? Let me set my goals to whatever I want, then I’ll add 2 stars.

title: Great App. Have two wishes

2. allow swiping between the pages. Since iPhone X this is the dominant system metaphor.
author: Ronbo999

title: Very well thought through
body:
I literally tested all the habit trackers (free and paid) in the app store and this one is the best because the designer spent time thinking things through. For example you can have badge numbers on the app icon showing you how many habits need to be checked off today. But you can also define between what times they should show so the app doesn’t nudge at times where you can’t actually do them. Details like this makes the app enjoyable. I planned to track only one habit and now ended up tracking 8 habits because it’s fun to do.

Tip: you can single press an icon to quickly swap through different visualizations. Long press on the calender visualization and you can edit it. Holding the little star in the lower right swaps all visualizations.

Feature request and 1 star less because:
- i wished there was a visualization of your streaks as a one year calendar view. At the moment i can only see either one full month or the diagram for longer periods. But the diagram doesn’t give me the precise data of a yearly calender view. A calender view is just more close to how I actually remember a particular week in a year opposed to a line on an cartesian coordinate system that goes up and down. Would be nice to have more visualization preferences or that you could see more visualizations when you scroll down in the ‘star’ view.

title: Please add the following features for individual tracking
body:
Dear streaks team,

Good app, indeed! However, there are several points I really wish to improve
When e.g. tracking vitamin C, I can specify a total amount of intake and how much a unit ist. E.g. I want to get 200mg of Vitamin C, where each Unit is 50. Could you do this also to the caffeine intake?
I write journal and I meditate, too. Two total different tasks, but they all count for me as mindful minutes. Currently, I cannot create two separate tasks that account for the journaling and meditation activity.  When e.g. Meditating 10 minutes as a task and writing journal 10 minutes. When I finish one of each other, then both are marked as finished. Could you make them as two separate mindful minutes activities?
It would be awesome deepen the integration to apple health.
Thank you!

Of course, it is still up to me to execute the tasks and to even open the app. But ones that bare motivation is there, Streaks is a great friend to keep me on track and move step by step, day by day towards a more fulfilling life.

Thank you, Felix.

title: Viele Möglichkeiten
body:
Ich habe mir Streaks aus dem Grund gekauft, weil ich ein bisschen Ordnung ins Leben bekommen wollte. Klar kann man auch einfach in den Kalender eintragen „24.01.2099 joggen gehen für 30 Min“ aber für komplexeres ist meiner Meinung nach der Apple Kalender nicht ausgelegt. Man kann sich bis zu 12 optionale Ziele setzen. Darunter gibt es ganz simple Dinge wie „Fitness“, „Joggen“ oder „nichts süßes gegessen“, aber es gibt sogar Ziele die man sich setzen kann wie „keine Finger gekaut“. Dazu kann man zwischen (ich schätze mal) 100- 200 Icons noch das passende Bild zum gewünschten Ziel heraussuchen bzw kann man auch seine Ziele selber benennen. 
Das Prinzip danach ist ganz einfach. Man nimmt sich beispielsweise vor, zwei mal die Woche 5 km joggen zu gehen. Jedes Mal, wenn man das Ziel erreicht hat, drückt man etwa 2 Sekunden auf das Icon und bekommt einen Punkt dafür. Hat man sein Wochenziel erreicht bekommt man einen Stern. Man kann sein Wochenziel natürlich auch toppen. Irgendwann rät einem die App doch mal sein Wochenziel zu erhöhen, wenn man viel Elan darin zeigt. Das kann man annehmen oder ablehnen. Ebenfalls kann man sich separat Uhrzeiten zu jedem Ziel festlegen, an denen man erinnert werden soll. 
Was ich mir noch wünsche, währe eine Funktion, dass man (ich arbeite Gleitschicht) jede Woche im Wechsel eine Woche morgens und eine Woche abends an seine Ziele erinnert wird. 
Fazit: super App, die tut, was sie tun soll, für den Preis natürlich ohne Werbung. Top 👍🏼

title: Jetzt schon besser!

Die App hatte ich schon länger und fand sie ziemlich cool. 
Was natürlich störte, war, das man maximal nur 6 Aufgaben gleichzeitiger haben konnte. 
Jetzt ist das ja endlich verbessert und man kann 12 Aufgaben haben. Das ist schon eine bessere Zahl.
Auch, dass die Aufgaben unterteilt sind ist sehr praktisch, so kann man zum Beispiel unter Arbeit und Lifestyle unterscheiden. 

Das Wechseln zwischen den Screens ist nicht so toll, das geht auf jeden Fall besser. 

Die anderen neuen Funktionen sind ganz nett. 

Nur das neue erste Einstellung-Menü ist sehr unpraktisch, da das da unten ziemlich eingequetscht ist. 
Das geht auch besser. 

Also zusammengefasst, fände ich es cool, man mit Swipen in den nächsten Screen kommt und das Menü besser wird. Zum Beispiel könnte man das Menü stapeln. 

Sonst ist es aber eine Super App und ich freue mich auf neue Funktionen. Macht weiter so!

title: Zu unflexibel
body:
Für den Preis von 3,99 EUR ist das Angebotene wirklich lächerlich und ebenso gut mit einer simplen Liste in der nativen Aufgaben-App vom iPhone zu erledigen. 

Frech finde ich, dass man auf nur 6 Aufgaben beschränkt wird, weil der Entwickler meint, dass man sich sonst schlecht auf mehrere Aufgaben konzentrieren könne. Halte ich für Unsinn. Gerade Kleinigkeiten, wie "10 Min. lesen" oder "Zähne putzen" sind ja wohl kaum solche Zeitfresser. 

Blöd auch, dass die Version für die Watch immer alle Aufgaben als Punkte in der Komplikationenansicht anzeigt. Also auch Aufgaben, die gar nicht heute anstehen, sondern für einen anderen Wochentag geplant sind. So sieht es immer so aus, als hätte man etwas nicht erledigt, weil die entsprechend nicht anstehende Aufgabe nicht als Punkt ausgeblendet wird. 

Im Übrigen ist mir die App bei der Planung viel zu unflexibel. Warum kann ich nicht sagen: "Zwei Mal pro Woche Sport" und dann schauen, wie ich das an welchem Wochentag zeitlich unterbringe? Nein, stattdessen muss ich im Vorhinein schon die Wochentage dafür festlegen. Das Programm ist ungefähr so flexibel, wie ein Fahrplan. Für meine Zwecke nicht zu gebrauchen!

Und die Übersetzung der Anleitung innerhalb der App ist übrigens einfach nur gruselig!!!

body:
Streaks is good overall, although the UI is non-standard as not as intuitive as it could be.

The ONE thing that keeps me from truly using it, is that it's seemingly only possible to track binary habits??

As in: "you did it today... or not".

You can't track something a la: "number of push-ups done today" or "hours worked towards goal X"

Really??? 🤷🏻‍♂️

So, for that I have to use an old app called Force of Habit that does it well. Would be nice if Streaks would implement such a basic, essential (!) method of building habits.

It's also way too easy to "fall off the waggon" with habits that are 100% binary. As an example: "Do 30 push-ups per day" breaks the streak if you one day only do 25 push-ups.

On the other hand, if your habit said "Push-ups per day" I know from my own experience that I'll some days do 40, 50, or more, push-ups. And the next day want to outdo myself, by doing more.

It's a more forgiving way to build habits, because you don't "break the chain" if you one day don't quite reach your goal. You could f.e. be down with flu, but still feel you're "doing the job / putting in the effort" by at least doing 5 push-ups, before going back to bed.

– What matters is you're _doing your best_ – right?

Which leads me to the following point:

Some days you feel like doing MORE than usual.

But if your habit in Streaks is a conservative "do 30 push-ups per day" you'll feel less inclined to do 40 or 50. Cos you're still "on paper" in Streaks checking/ticking off that you've done 30. Cos Streaks is Binary... 😏🙄

Fact is, it's more motivating when it matters HOW much effort you put in.

title: Warning: Avoid the macOS version

The temporary directory created by Streaks had to be removed using macOS Recovery Mode. Hint: Look for com.streaksapp.streaks in /private/var/folders if this happens to you.

title: Apps do not create habits. Use a sticky note.
body: I was super excited when I purchased this, and I also submitted a 5 star review. That was 6 months ago. Now, whenever I look at it, I feel a bit stupid. I think most of us have 'habit issues' at some level. So, when an app comes along and promises to help, we get excited because, subconsciously, we imagine that the app is going to do what we haven't been able to do ourselves. We imagine our new, improved selves, and our brains are flooded with dopamine in anticipation of this bright future. But it doesn't work like that. The app can't change your habits, only you can. At the end of the day, I have not managed to stick to a single one of the habits I've listed in Streaks. It's not the app's fault as such. It's just plain phychology. Installing the app is no different from making New Year's resolutions - and we all know how well they work. My advice: Write your goals / habits on a piece of paper and stick it somewhere where you will see it all the time. That constant reminder is going to be a lot more effective than an app, which, after a while, you'll mostly likely just start ignoring. And, in fact, when you start to fail at your 'streaks', you'll experience negative cognitive feedback, which is counter productive because 'failure' is demotivating. Pen and paper going forward! Good luck :-)

title: It is a super app, but there are too few categories (only 12)
body:
I absolutely love this app. It combines features of a to-do list with that of a done list, and can help manage habit stacks, not just individual habits. 

I have been looking for something like this for, literally, years. 

The app has an intuitive minimalistic interface. And it is super easy to use once you have sorted out what you need to get done into categories or habit stacks. It lets you choose an icon for each habit (stack), so all you life is literally summarised pictorially if you have taken your time to categorise everything (I have spent about two hours). 

I hope that in the future it will be possible either to add more sets of 6 tasks/habits/habit (stacks), or to give each habit (stack) a much longer description, specifying how many times and how often you should do each task or in which order the tasks should be done within each category. Or both. 

For example, I would like to go outside every day. To make it more productive, I specify the number of steps I have to make, the number of pics to take (I usually create a blog entry with the pics, so the whole thing is more fun: it was difficult to think of a good reason to go out when I worked from home, so now I have something to look forward to). But on some days I have more time. On those days I go on longer walks and listen to audiobooks. So this whole thing is one complex habit stack. It would be great if it were possible to add its description as a single habit (stack) or category, one if the six in a set, and not break it down into smaller ones. 

Thank you for the great app! I will recommend it to all my friends.

title: Mi solución definitiva.
body: Para personas que quieren hacer su vida mucho más productiva añadiendo buenas costumbres o simplemente hábitos diarios que suelen olvidarse, esta app es la solución definitiva. Con su simple pero muy personalizarles interfaz, he conseguido centrarme en lo que más importa en mi vida y olvidarme de muchas malas costumbres. Llevo varios meses con ella y es genial. Todos los días reservo cinco minutos para revisarla y ver qué cosas he hecho y cuáles no. La recomiendo a cualquiera que tenga muchas cosas en la cabeza, pero que quiera llevarlas todas a cabo, especialmente las costumbres. El precio sin lugar a dudas vale todos sus céntimos.

- le design 
- les chrono type pomodoro intégré 
- l’intégration des donnés health 
- Jusqu’à 4 pages de 6 objectifs chacun 

Il me manque 

- la possibilité de nommer chacune des 4 pages 
- une visibilité accrue des objectifs atteints , on voit des points, des courbes mais qui ne me parle que pas. Ex j’ai un objectifs de 100 km à vélo par semaine . On voit bien un cercle qui se remplit mais pas le chiffre précis et une fois atteint on voit plus aucun chiffre de la distance parcouru

- connection avec l'application santé ce qui évite de saisir les données (comme par exemple le nombre de pad dans la journée)

Les défauts que j'avais notés ont été corrigés :
- on n'est plus limité à 6 objectifs (mais 12, cela me suffit !)

title: Too expensive for what it is
body:
I paid 6 GPB for this app and must say I‘m massively disappointed by the quality considering the price point. 
The theme is barely customizable - the only wallpapers I liked color wise had emoji style watermarks. Why can’t I just take a photo as a wallpaper or choose my own colors with fades or disable the watermarks?
The user experience is terrible - considering this should be an intuitive and simple app it takes too long to figure out in which case the the dots are responsive and which case  they aren‘t. I only use the app to track one thing, so the Up Next feature was confusing and it took me 20 minutes to figure out what it was. Moreover, I wish there were more actual icons. The data visualization for the stats for me and my friend who shared a task with me could be improved. Lastly, it looks like there‘s a bug where if you set the color for the icon you cannot unset it anymore - the icon is permanently filled. 
Overall, great if the app only cost 2 GBP but considering this is supposedly the market leader for habit tracking apps it‘s really bad and too expensive. Very disappointing.

title: Great concept, unreliable sync
body:
The Streaks app offers a fantastic concept for habit tracking, but its execution falls short. Synchronisation between the Apple Watch, iPhone, and Mac is frustratingly unreliable. Tasks completed on the Apple Watch frequently fail to update on other devices, and activity ring progress doesn’t show correctly on the watch. Likewise Mac or iPhone to the watch. 

This is particularly disappointing given that iCloud sync is enabled on all devices, background app refresh is on, and the devices are connected to fast, reliable Wi-Fi. Considering the small amount of data being transferred when a task is completed, the sync issues are difficult to excuse.

Support was unhelpful, even infering they don’t have an Apple Watch for testing. While the idea is solid, the app's poor sync and lack of refinement make it hard to recommend in its current state.

title: Useful For My Needs & Good Price But With Slight Annoyances
body:
Useful app that wasn’t too expensive or had a subscription. I can’t remember things easily so I wanted a way to add reminders to my phone so that they would remind me all day and count different meditations etc using the Dynamic Island and Lock Screen as a permanent reminder.

Unfortunately while this app does seem to use the Dynamic Island it (as far as I can tell) is only if you are currently running a time based Streak that has a timer that has actually been started. You can’t manually choose to keep a reminder or a none time based Streak in the Dynamic Island or in a persistent notification to remind yourself throughout the day.

The lock screen medication countdowns are useful ie so I can see that I have 3 of 4 tablets left today etc but it’s a bit annoying having multiple and not being able to specify which ones I want to see and when.

I found a slight workaround that involves using different pages for different streaks and then hiding the ones that I don’t need to see so that they won’t show on my Lock Screen or in widgets etc, but I think that’s more annoying than just being able to use a menu option to exclude certain Streaks from your screen.

Same goes for manually updating ones with multiple sections throughout the day like if I forgot to log 3 tablets then why I can’t just manually set the amount instead of having to manually press it for each missed time, which is even more annoying when you make a mistake and have to go through even more unnecessary steps to undo and then redo it all again…

I really hope this is possible in a future update because it seems easy enough to do considering the current settings allow for certain Streaks that persist on your screen, widgets, notifications and in the Dynamic Island but you get little control over how and when and which are shown without hiding them completely.

Despite this I still found the widgets useful and visual enough that they work as great reminders throughout the day and useful logs over time and I can quickly visualise how many tablets I have taken / are remaining and see it on my Apple Watch.

I love the Shortcuts integration too which fit right into an existing Shortcut I had made to log medication. Before I had struggled to find a way to log my total daily dose and then to count down every time I logged a tablet and some days I take more which other apps couldn’t handle without ruining the daily amount but Streaks can.

Please expand on this customisation and make it so you can select which streaks to use in the shortcut even if they are completed that day and allow us to manually choose which Streaks appear especially in the Dynamic Island and for how long they persist. If I could do that then this would the perfect app and hopefully with future updates it will be.

title: Great app that’s flexible at the cost of a little confusion
body:
I’ve not come up with a goal I want to track yet that I can’t do in Streaks. It’s great at nudging me into good habits.

This flexibility comes at the cost of a UI that’s sometimes pretty confusing. For example, it’s not particularly intuitive to know that you can cycle between states from the calendar view if you normally use the gauge view. However, the overall experience is great.

Best way I’ve found so far to use the gamified approach of Brilliant or Duolingo to keep you motivated to build a habit or complete a long task.
author: _urfolomeus

title: Much more than a simple task-tracking tool
body:
Streaks makes tracking completed tasks an absolute breeze. The app is well-designed, with a brilliantly intuitive (and good-looking) interface, so that core functionality is pretty much entirely self-explanatory.

That’s an achievement by itself, but what really blew me away was how deeply customisable, flexible, and powerful the app is if you take a bit of time to dive into the menus and explore what it’s really capable of: custom task scheduling, automatic reminders, finding trends in completion data, the list of features goes on and on.

One of the very few apps I use every day, and I’ve come to rely on Streaks to manage much of my day-to-day work both personally and professionally. 

Absolute gem of an app.

title: Game changer
body: My mate recommended this app and I was slightly dubious, but it really has changed my life. I’m always starting a fitness regimen and I forget to do it for 2 days, then it’s gone and all the hard work is wasted. This app has made me form good habits and I don’t want to start from zero again…so I do my exercises regardless of time of night, mindset or tiredness. title: Well thought out, with limitations
body:
Takes a while to find where everything is, some features are relatively hidden, which isn’t great for UX. The features and functionality present are well thought out. But for the cost, it should not be artificially limiting its users to 24 total active tasks. I can see the limit used to be 12, which would be inexcusable. I can understand how a limit can force the user to decide what’s actually important - but that’s not something the app should impose upon paying customers. 

It would be good to have a habit for a certain medication being taken x times per week. Although this is a restriction on Apple’s Health API.

title: The Best App in the Store
body: As someone who has dedicated much of my personal, academic & professional life researching into the flow state, I can unquestionably say this is my favourite app… ever! In fact with all the advances in AI, I was seriously considering ditching Apple, but this app made me think twice, syncing so brilliantly as it does with the Watch. Every day I wake up to the same blank slate, then tick off my vitamins and supplements, it automatically registers when I’ve used my Bluetooth scales, and then it’s workout time, I burn 700 calories before I sit at my computer ( which is ok when I’m nearly touching 70 in a couple of weeks) then I tick off ‘homework’, two sets of three pomodoro sessions, three sets of twenty minutes of reading/studying… oh and I take at least one photo before I go home, where I check off some house cleaning and two sessions of playing a musical instrument… oh and it also tracks when I wash my hands, so I set a minimum of seven times a day. I only just discovered that it also has some fantastic watch faces which I have just installed. These are just my preferences but there are loads to choose from, many of them no brainers and all of them allowing you to set an easily achievable threshold and see it slowly increase automatically over the forthcoming weeks and months. Guys, if you wanna beta tester, I’m well up for it, you may even convince me to save up for one of these new VR headsets… I can’t imagine how good this app will be when you’re wearing one of those!

title: i love that its simple and free

allow to add a task/habit without a specific goal or target. e.g. I take ADHD meds as needed so i don’t really have a goal, i just want to know how often i take them. (also, tracking habits without a goal, for people with mental health issues, just helps them know if they’ve generally been “feeling good” or “feeling bad” as sometimes we can’t tell) 

in the help section, when you mention a specific button, like “Up Next” or sth, adding a photo of the button somewhere helps “visual people” remember it better so they can find it easier and use it. 

what i love: the release notes, the help section, being able to change when the habits reset, the many icons and colour changes, being able to add a note to a task, and the task reports. 

brilliant app!! good job 👍

title: More screens is a must for some users
body:
I appreciate the ideal of focusing on only 12 habits and can see that some UI currently hinges on the two screens. But it feels arbitrary to not have the option to add additional screens if I need them, and the option would do no harm to anyone that can manage with the default two screens.

Alongside other habits, I wanted to track weekly streaks for running, cycling and swimming targets, but tracking their streaks individually uses up a quarter of all my slots. Why should someone that runs three days a week have more other habit slots to track with than someone that does three different exercises per week? I also wanted to track sleep as when I go to bed and when I wake up, rather than just overall time so I can see where I’m missing my targets. I find that habits work for me when I can focus on specific details, but I’m having to generalise or cut other things out to make space.

I really like the way the app works in general, and to be honest I’d pay for additional screens or a second instance of the same app just to track what I want. Compromising on what details I can track is a real frustration though, and I do regret paying for it at the moment rather than finding an app with no limits. I’ve already spent time setting up shortcuts and some habits so I’ll cross my fingers for an improvement while I test out other apps for a secondary/replacement tracker.

author: 245bob

title: Outstanding
body:
I’ve tried a lot of habit trackers and this is the best. 

There has clearly been a lot of love and thought put into this app.

It’s incredibly streamlined and pulling data from Apple Health to automatically tick off habits like Meditation, Work Outs, Sleep, Running ect is absolutely genius. 

The developers are clearly interested in how the app will actually improve your life. Not just making something pretty. Tracking & improving 12 habits is more than enough for anyone serious about being a better version of themselves and it’s refreshing to see the developers not be influenced to increase this. 

The widgets are also outstanding, the watch app is slightly squashed but also excellent. 

Best 5 bucks you will ever spend.

Even after 1 day of using this app I felt very motivated to make sure I kept my streak of 100% completion going, the simple visual design makes progress easy to monitor and makes it fun to complete

The ability to have 2 separate pages of 6 tasks is also very handy 

Highly recommend!

On a similar vein, it would be nice if the widget could hide tasks that weren’t applicable to that day too.
author: emkay_online

title: Really like the app
body:
Update: the recent update seems to have broken the glass-by-glass counter of the water category. Now it checks of the activity when I am trying to tick only one glass. And even if I manually mark this task as incomplete, the app completes it itself. Not sure if this has something to do with the sync with Apple Watch, which has been the only thing that has changed for me. But uninstalling the app from the watch has also not helped. Hopefully this gets corrected soon

- 
Review besides the bug below:

The concept of streaks is really solid to form habits. It’s a psychological hack, yes, but something that works for me. Mind you an app is not as powerful as a poster in a room, but its the next best thing.

I have had a few apps which track streaks, and this app, Streaks, definitely has the best design that actually is close to checking out things on a poster. And UI really is important to promote usage and habit building.

The cool things which this app does differently which stood out for me:
1: you can set timers for timed activities like 1 hour study or 15 min meditation.
2. Multiple tasks which form an activity can be broken down. For e.g, drinking 10 glasses of water can be checked off one glass at a time.
3. There’s a tie in to health app so you don’t need to check off workouts and other health things.

Overall happy with this app and see myself using it. I have had a few streaks going the last couple of months, but have not been consistent enough. Hope that will change in the coming months.

author: joshyboy1985

title: Got me right on track!
body:
Nothing even close to negative to say about this app, it has put my life totally back on track. That may sound sad but it's true, it's miraculous what a little star with a rising number can do when it's next to a habit you're trying to improve on.

Simple to use, about four billion theme options so the right colour hits you in the feels when it's time to clock in on your particular habit and an interface which sends a crisp high five to those little OCD sections of your brain each time you succeed.

Solid performance, works seamlessly with Apple Watch and costs much less than the sinking feeling of failure you get when you let your plans go to the wall each night.

If I could make one change, it'd be the ability to check the habits lined up for tomorrow, but without that it's still a thing of beauty.

author: JN-37

title: Great app
body: I found this at just the right time. I tried it a while ago but didn’t really get into it. Now, combined with a genuine desire to create better habits, this app is really coming into its own. The only thing which I would like to see done differently is I would like an option to have more than 12 on the go at one time. This may be controversial, and I can see the reasons behind having only 12. So, perhaps a compromise add functionality without tempting the user to create too many habits at once could be the ability to group clusters of related habits together. For example, I am trying to develop a reading habit for both fiction and non-fiction and so I have both of these as habits to track. If I could, for example, click on “reading“ and have two connected habits open up as options, that would be really cool. At the moment, one can create clusters of habits by, for example, calling the habit “read fiction, read non-fiction“ and just putting the habit as two sessions per day, but that is crude and unwieldy and doesn’t show if you missed one and not the other. Habit clusters would be awesome. Anyway, that would be the improvement I would really like to see, and that would make the tracker even more useful than it already is.

body:

I’ve found that most others you have to set a time to be notified, and I’ve never found that helpful as I start to expect it so get into the habit of ignoring it, whereas because this app decides when to notify me it feels like a genuine reminder.  Such a simple thing, yet so important. I like how customisable it is too, with all of the different icons, and how it integrates with my Apple Watch. I also appreciate that it’s a one time payment only, as I refuse to purchase subscriptions as it’s a rip off. 

The only downside to the app for me is that I expected it to be a little more goals oriented, which is probably just my misunderstanding but it is a small disappointment. I thought I’d be able to use it to plan out and track my progress towards large goals, but it’s basically a habit tracker.

body:

It wasn’t until a good few years later after reading Atomic Habits that I went back to it as a habit tracker. It’s very powerful and helpful for this and I would highly recommend reading that book first then using the app. It really goes hand in hand and makes so much sense now. I’m achieving new habits and I’m noticing the positive changes that come with it. Today the app congratulated me for doing meditation each morning and even suggested I add another minute to achieve even better results! Great stuff.

title: Great for habit building
body:
This app gives you a straightforward and simple way to track your progress on habit building. Made reading daily much easier and had given me another incentive to want to read. Seeing the streak number go up is rewarding and motivating to keep going. 

However, warning: this does not immediately make you more productive. It is merely a way to see your progress and a reminder on what you want to make a habit. 

In my opinion, adding 6 streaks straight off the bat is a bad idea. It will be almost impossible, as i figured out myself, to start 6 streaks in one go. It is far better to start one or two streaks and add more as the initial streaks become engrained into your day to day life.

body:

The interface is smart, the Apple Watch app works really well, and using the bundle app (Health Face) has been great for showing up my remaining calories on the Apple Watch too.

Great work, and so much better having a fair single purchase price than all these premium subscriptions, great decision by the developers.

The developers have addressed this by stating that it wouldn’t be wise to set too many tasks for them to be achieved but I think that’s really a call the user should make. At the very least, there should be 3 pages so that the user can split tasks into morning, daytime and evening or perhaps daily, weekly and monthly. It is a great app though so I definitely do not regret the purchase but I do hope the developers consider and add page function going forward.

author: JustNicks

title: Fantastic app - one gaping hole
body: First things first, I'd like to say that this app is little by little changing my life. So far it has helped my kick coffee, alcohol and smoking once and for all, start meditating and exercising daily and much more. I'm not one for reviews and the fact that I'm reviewing it is testament to it's simple brilliance - and I've tried every habit tracking and to do list app there is. However for me the fact you can only have 12 tasks is becoming a real hindrance. I understand the rationale - the idea is to focus on a small number of important habits at a time rather than overwhelm yourself. However, once having internalised a habit and moving onto a new one, I still want to track my old habits (to keep me from slipping up - eg having a cigarette socially. Currently one of the screens is used up with bad habits and the other with good, but I cannot add more and so my self improvement has stopped. Please add the option to add more habits ! I'd happily pay for additional screens!

title: Would be perfect with a couple of updates
body:
Just started using this today, and it’s good. It took a few minutes to figure things out, as it’s not completely intuitive. I like it’s simplicity and the UI is very nice. 

Little things that would make this perfect for me:

- Switching between pages by swiping left and right, instead of having to tap an icon. It would just feel better. 

- The ability to log “extra” completions of habits. For instance, let’s say my goal is to do yoga once a week, but I end up doing it three times in one week. It would be really nice to be able to log that, instead of the app preventing it. It would be even better if the app made a big deal of it by tracking “extra” completions in a different colour, or something similar.

body:

Thank you for not charging a subscription - software is not a service and I’m very happy to pay once, which I believe is a large aspect of your success over similar apps that require subscriptions.

Two changes I would like to see are:

1) Allowing more than twelve habits, and perhaps to be able to display more on-screen at once.

2) Setting a number of times a week for negative tasks. For example, I’d like to limit drinking to one night per week, but being a student it’s not very predictable what night that will be. At the moment I have to check  ‘don’t drink’ 6 days a week, but I would rather just uncheck it once per week on the day I do drink.

Do you guys think you’d be able to implement these things?

title: Good app
body:
Handles whatever kind of task you could want, in one clunky but functional package.

Pros:
• iCloud sync.
• Broad Health support for automatic completion of tasks.
• Extensive (notification & theme) customisation.
• Universal app support (iPad, iPhone, Watch).

Technical limitation?:
• Health data retrieval (& sync) requires specifically launching the iPhone version of the app, not iPad or Watch.

Cons:
• The interface can be quite opaque, with ‘…’ buttons everywhere.
• No iCloud sync for per-task notification settings.
• Some bugs. (With Health sleep data permission granted - adding a sleep duration task works fine, but the wake & sleep task says no data is available and doesn't update from Health)

Worth reading the help section of the app to reveal a few extra details, such as shake-to-undo.

title: Good, but could be better
body:
Don't get me wrong, this is a good app for making good habits. It makes it easy to mark a habit as complete so that it isn't a chore to keep track of.

It isn't very good at tracking bad habits though. I would expect a better way of tracking when you have not done something, as if you were trying to break a bad habit. All you would need to do is reverse the colours for bad habits, so you mark off when you have done something you shouldn't have, by the end of the week you will be able to see how often you did the bad habit, and will be able to see how you progress over time. 

It also doesn't make much sense to limit the number of tasks to 6. I know many people won't need to track more than that but what if they do? It seems kinda arbitrary to have a limit like this. I assume it is something to do with fitting all of the buttons in the today widget, but surely you could add as many as you like in the app and just mark up to 6 to be shown in the today widget?

Anyway, those are my suggestions. It's a good app, but I can see where it could be improved.

title: Life changing
body:
By using this app everyday I have changed my life. When you're on day 67 of physical exercise and you're feeling tired there is no way you're going to miss a day and go back to zero. If you use this app diligently your life will change 🙌🏾  
I have checked many ritual building apps after reading the life changing "POWER OF FULL ENGAGEMENT" book and this is without doubt the best. Choosing just 6 behaviours makes you focused on actually getting them installed into your life as effortless as brushing your teeth rather than having a huge unmanageable list (as I have done). The feature of having stats for the last month and last 7 days is also exactly on point. Many others give you your stats since the birth of the app which means if you fall off for 4 months you can never get to the rewarding acknowledgment of high percentages. 

Thank you STREAK team for a such a simple, beautiful, elegant and compelling solution to installing rituals into ones life. You are providing a powerful infrastructure for people to make incredible change and do good work in the world. Keep doing what you're doing 🙏🏾✨👊🏾

body:

The idea is that you can set targets to achieve (mine are all daily) and you can work towards them during the day however you please. Then every time you manage to achieve the target by the time you set, you build up your streak. The best thing, for me, is the flexibility compared to usual timetable type apps! 

Because you're doing things daily, it also regulates your daily activities, which is a helpful bonus. 

I should mention though that I got this app free from a Starbucks card, so with that in consideration, I have no complaints!

title: Backtrack?
body:
It's an awesome app. Really simple and easy to use.
You can use it to aim for daily tasks or set it for only certain days or number of days per week. An improvement would be the option of aiming for twice a day.
It would also be good if you could pull up a calendar and record for previous days so that if you've forgotten to log it but have done the task, then you don't lose your streak. Or be able to say 'my current streak is two days' when you create a new task. I understand that 6 is a good amount of habits for most people, and the option for too many would be overwhelming but I use it to track the most basic things (shower, clean teeth, etc) so having a few more would be good. Maybe 8 (4 rows of 2) or 9 (3 rows of 3) so that they still all fit on the same page.
