title: Simple and very effective
body:
This is a brilliant app, especially when used with the Apple Watch complication. It's a very simple and effective way of monitoring your daily habits and ensuring you get them done. Basically this app will improve your life. Not bad for a couple of quid! 

The health kit integration works well, although I would like a bit more granularity in the goals you can set- eg being able to choose a target of 4500 steps rather than just 4000 or 5000. Also, the only frustration I have with the Apple Watch compilation is that it doesn't seem to auto update health data connected habits unless you open the iPhone app first. 

As someone who likes to tinker, I'd like to be able to try out other habits to track without having to delete one of my six current habits (and all their historical data) first. 

And possibly I'd also like the ability to put habits on hold for a holiday. Maybe make it so that the minimum hold length is 5 days. I'm not expecting to go to bed on time, read every day, run every day, on my holiday, so I don't really want to feel bad about not completing them... But maybe this suggested hold period be too tempting for some people. 

Long story short it's excellent, and only a few minor minor things above would make it perfect.

title: The most powerful and helpful app for building consistency in passion, and creating desired habits
body:
I’ve been trying to be productive and improve myself for almost 10 years now. Have tried many methods, apps, techniques, books, etc. I’ve become very productive for sure, but still I couldn’t become consistent in the things I wanted to do or I loved to do. Then enters this app in my life because of randomly searching productive apps to overcome my current weaknesses. It quickly became one of my most favourite app of these last 10 years. Streak numbers tell me how long I have come, and force me to continue my desired habits Continue in a healthy way. I can see my progress, edit my progress I missed to log by mistake, I can prioritise my habits by dragging them in different pages like first page for number 1 priority task, second for secondary priority tasks and so on. Ask though every single feature is my favourite, I want to give special thanks to shortcut feature. I created custom shortcuts using shortcut app, to start timer, close other apps, directly open desired app or multiple apps to work on that habit. For example: when I click on reading habit, it’ll close all other apps, start timer for few minutes or 1 pomodoro, open current book and current page, and silent notifications,etc. all in just one click from this Streak app itself. Now I don’t feel the need to create bookmark or move required aid to Homescreen. I just love this shortcut feature.

Improvement Suggestion: please give two different options to write shortcut name in habit setting. One for Mac shortcut name, one for I/Os shortcut name. So that when I click habit from Mac, it will run Mac shortcut. And if i run for m from iOS or iPadOS, it will run iOS shortcut. Because same created shortcut will be synced to all devices and streak habit will run shortcut on iOS/iPadOS properly but not in Mac as Mac shortcut and I/Os shortcuts are different. Currently it shows error.
Now i have disabled icloud sync of shortcuts and then edited mac shortcuts according to Mac. So it’s working for now. But Please find a workable solution for above mentioned issue. 

Thank you very much for creating such an amazing simple, intuitive and great app with awesome user experience.
Keep up the good work.

title: Repetition without logic
body:
You do 6 exercises daily. There are 4 levels to suit everyone’s convenience and body strength. It’s a good app to form daily habits but that’s the end of good part. 

Now the bad part.
There is no provision for breaks. So you do exercises one after the other without even 1 second of break in between. You can pause the timer but there is no in built break system. Then comes the part where they make you do the same exercise one after the other for short duration. So 5 push-ups, then 10 push-ups and 2 pushes rather than say, 10 push-ups and 7 push-ups consecutively. The problem is one has to focus again on the same exercise multiple time for short durations than for longer time but fewer times. I don’t get the logic. 
My last review was equally critical but never got published. I hope this one does.

title: Great application!
body:
First, I underestimated its impact. People talk about gamification and other buzz words, but these folks have shown how that can be used to help improve our habits. For the first time in my life, I have continuously brushed before I sleep 90 percent of the time in the past month. Even my walking and reading habits have improved. This app genuinely benefitted me. Thanks for that.

Next, I am a designer myself and I think that this app is well designed. It looks ookay, but every detail that is needed to do what you have to is taken care of. The options are never in sight until needed, but are obvious when you need them. For instance, after adding my tasks to walk, read and brush, I realized that I have to reminded of these at different times (evening, before I sleep and after dinner). When I searched, the option was there. Similarly, these days, I brush but forget to mark it before I sleep. The next day, when I open the app and try to mark, it asks me about the day before too. Similarly, when I've consistently met my walking target, it asked me if it should increase the daily target steps. Thats neat!

I don't usually write long reviews, but this app deserves it!

title: Clever, inventive, simple
body:
The App is very nice, a clever implementation of a simple but habit-changing idea. Not overly intuitive to set the first time, but very useful and pleasant in general. It really helped me in establishing good habits, especially not health of fitness related ones, which tend to be covered already by other Apps and Apple Watch functionalities.

Edit: the App used to have a huge problem of sync with the Apple Watch, but it has since then been updated and the problem is solved. It now works very well in sync with Apple Watch, which renders very easy to start and complete activities on the fly. The score of my review is now updated accordingly.

title: must!
body: Dovrebbe essere installata di default sul sistema perché si integra alla perfezione con l'app salute ed apple watch. Incarna perfettamente la filosofia Apple: bella, semplice e funzionale. Ero in dubbio se spendere i circa 5,00 euro, ma è fatta davvero bene e non me ne sono pentito. Ne ho provate alcune gratuite che funzionavano allo stesso modo..ma l'occhio appagato e la semplicità di utilizzo fanno la differenza. Dal punto di vista tecnico l'app è più elastica di quanto espresso nella sua presentazione, sono possibili infatti diverse configurazioni (per esempio quante volte in un determinato periodo) delle varie abitudini (buone o cattive)e delle notifiche che si vogliono ricevere. Sull'orologio apple è davvero funzionale ed intuitiva. Un esempio della sua integrazione? l'acqua bevuta come buona abitudine viene inserita nell'app salute in nutrizione..oppure se si fanno i respiri yoga coll'orologio viene contata come fatta e viceversa..si integra persino con gli anelli delle attività!! La facilità d'uso è un requisito essenziale per il tipo di app, inserire una cosa fatta o non fatta e capire cosa manca alla nostra giornata é un attimo!

body:

完了していないタスクが1つのページ(6つのタスクページ)の中にあれば、他のタスクが完了していたとしても、終わっていないタスクのページが表示されていたが、別のページが表示されるようになった。

title: Former fan, now in total dismay
body:
I have used Streaks for some years, and it has become an important part of my struggle to lead a healthy and balanced lifestyle. It worked fine for a long time but about a year ago it started randomly deleting tasks, sometimes replacing them with others that were already there, leading to duplicates. The thing has gone haywire. I repeatedly contacted the makers, and though they express sympathy, they are totally unable to fix what ought to be a fairly simple problem. I am deeply, deeply disappointed and looking for a replacement app.

Update:About a year later, the same old bug has started messing everything up again. Truly pathetic that it still has not been fixed.And yes I have checked but I am on the latest version. 10.07.

Update: Another year has passed and the problem of this bug that randomly deletes icons and data still remains unresolved. Utter rubbish.
author: konwajiro

title: Suggestion for Allowing Additional Entries After Goal Completion
body:
I’ve been using Streak and love how it helps me stay consistent with my daily habits. However, I’ve noticed that once I reach my daily goal (e.g., 3 times), I can’t log any additional entries for the same day.

It would be incredibly helpful if users could continue logging entries even after completing their goals. This feature would allow us to track extra efforts or overachievement without altering the original goal settings.

I hope you’ll consider adding this functionality in a future update. Thank you for creating such a great app!

title: 大好きなアプリですが、改善してほしい。I love it very much, but would like to see improvements.
body:
I would be more than happy if you could implement the following points

-When a task requires 3 actions per day, I would like it to be possible to count the number of actions taken more than 3 times, e.g. 4 or 5 times. I would like to see a record kept even if less than three actions are taken, for example, if only two or one action is taken.
-About the Pomodoro timer. I would like the number of times to concentrate to be counted even after the number of times has been achieved. Also, I would like the number of times I have concentrated to be counted even if I have not achieved the number of times.
-For tasks linked to health care. For example, for a step count task, I would like the number of steps taken to be recorded regardless of whether the task was completed or not.
-I would like the above three points to be reflected in the summary graph.
-I would like a simple count up and count down function.

This is because I want to check later with the graph function how much I concentrated on a task or how much I could not concentrate on a task. With the current specs, there is a problem when a task is not completed. That is, it is not possible to tell whether I did not do the task at all, or whether I did a little bit of the task.

I would like to see an improvement.

以下の点を実装してくれると、もっと嬉しいです。

-1日3回行動したら達成、というような内容のタスクの時。3回以上行動した場合、例えば4回や5回行動したことをカウントできるようにして欲しい。行動が3回未満であった場合も、例えば2回や1回しか行動しなかった場合であっても、記録は残して欲しい。
-ポモドーロタイマーについて。集中する回数は、回数を達成した後もカウントできるようにして欲しい。また、回数を達成できなかった場合も、何回集中したのかカウントしてほしい。
-ヘルスケアと連動したタスクの場合。例えば歩数のタスクについて、達成できていても、達成できていなくても、歩数は記録して欲しい。
-上記3点を、サマリーのグラフに反映して欲しい。
-単純なカウントアップ、カウントダウンの機能が欲しい。

これは、どれだけタスクに集中したか、もしくは集中できなかったか、後からグラフ機能で確認したいからです。今の仕様だと、タスクを完了できなかった時に問題があります。それは、タスクを全くやらなかったのか、それとも、少しだけタスクをこなしたのか、の判別がつかないことです。

改善を望みます。

However, there are some bugs I hope to be repaired for continuous use.
1. Sound of some habits could not be changed. Even though I have changed them all at once, some of them remain the original sound and cannot be changed independently as well.

Besides, it would be better if it could have an all black background both on iPhone and Apple Watch without the icons turning white(now the icons on watch become white when the background on iPhone’s Streaks is selected black), so that the color display on different devices could keep same.

title: Impressive!
body:
I had been looking for an app that would help me keep on top of things I need to do but tend to forget, now that I am in my 80s. In “Streaks” I found it. Deceptively simple and effective in use, and visually very attractive, it has a wealth of options “under the hood” that repay careful investigation. For example, it can handle tasks that need to be performed several times a day or only once or twice a week. It can even handle bad habits that shouldn’t be indulged—ever! It’s also worth noting that a total of 12 tasks (on two screens showing six each) can now be handled, and it offers integration with Apple Watch and the Health App!

Added later: I should add that all the screens for both display and control are simple, clear, intuitive and attractive. That’s a very rare combination.

title: タスクが12個までというのが残念！
body:
シンプルでUIも良く、日々達成感を得られてモチベーション維持に役立ちます！
が、多くの方が言っている通り、タスクが12個までという制限がなんとも。
（書き出してみると12個なんてあっという間です！）
タスク数に制限がなければ朝昼夜、曜日別にリストを作って日々フレッシュに過ごせるのですが。私は日毎に家の中の掃除する場所をタスク化して管理したかったので、残念です。他に、子供達とのやりとり、仕事の経費関係、ワークアウト、美容などなど。

600円も払っているのだから
そこは頑張ってもらいたかったかなー。

title: ヘルスケアと連動したタスクAPP
body:
ヘルスケア、その他のワークアウトAppと連動しているので、手入力でタスクを終了する場面が少ない。
ここが一番重要で、タスクAPPの難点といえば、「タスクAPPを開いて処理すること」だった。
まさに本末転倒。
このAppは楽にタスク処理できるし、視覚(UIがオシャレ)・聴覚(タスク完了時のサウンドを選べる)で楽しめるので、難なく続けれています。
セッティングを上手くやれば、あとは自分が行動するのみ！！

body:

週に何回かの単位でやること、
毎日やることなどをタスクごとに分けることができ、

私は必ずやりたいタスクの他に、写真を撮る、というタスクもいれていて（アプリにおすすめされた）

title: Good!!
body:
使い始めは「こんなもんか…」とか思ってました。しかし、ここ一ヶ月くらい使ってみての感想なんですが、シンプルなデザインとリマインダー機能、それに指定の時間がきたら通知してくれたりと、使いやすくて本当に助かっています！！
自分は勉強や筋トレが続かない性格なんですが、このアプリで少し治った気がします笑
どれくらい継続できてるのかとかの機能は、ほかのアプリでも探せばいくらでも出てきます。が、大切なのは続くかどうかって事です。他のアプリも散々試してきました。時には有料のを買って後悔したこともあります…このアプリに最終的に落ち着いて他のは全部消しちゃいましたてけど笑笑
リマインダー機能、どれくらい続いているのかの継続記録の機能、シンプルなデザイン、凝った使用。全部好きです！！

title: 너무 좋아요!
body:
잘 쓰고 있습니다! 간단하게 보기 좋은 것 같아요.
그런데 습관들의 순서를 바꿀 수 있으면 좋겠어요. 그리고 위쪽에 다음이라는 순서가 하나만 설정되는데 그게 아니라 여러 아이콘들이 있고 그중에 골라서 갈 수 있으면 좋겠어요. 그리고 선택적으로 페이지를 넘기면 제가 설정한 카테고리만큼 페이지수를 늘릴 수 있으면 좋겠고 페이지를 넘겼을 때 카테고리별로 볼 수 있는 기능도 있으면 좋겠어요. 그리고 메인 화면에 설정, 페이지 확인, 별표 말고 달력 아이콘을 하나 더 넣어서 달력 아이콘만 누르면 카테고리별로라고 혹은 모든 작업들 리스트가 뜨는데 그걸 누르면 깔끔하게 달력만 볼 수 있는 기능도 있으면 좋을 것 같아요.

생활 루틴같은걸 너무 타이트하게 목매이지 않게 하면서도 알림같은걸로 계속 리마인드 시켜줌

가령 10분 책읽기를 일주일동안 못하면 9분으로 줄일까요라고 물어봐줌

Focus To-Do 라는 뽀모도로앱 처럼 소리가나면 이 앱 하나만으로 제 인생을 해결 할 수 있을거같아요 부틱드립니다 업데이트 ㅠㅡㅠㅡㅠ 제발!!!!

### 영어 (English):
Everything is great, but I would love it if there were sounds when using the Pomodoro timer.

Sounds like ticking, wind, or nature sounds, etc.

If there were sounds like in the Focus To-Do Pomodoro app, I feel like this app would solve my life. Please, I beg you for an update, ㅠㅡㅠㅡㅠ please!!!

### 스페인어 (Español):
Todo está bien, pero me encantaría que hubiera sonidos cuando uso el temporizador Pomodoro.

Sonidos como el tic-tac, el viento, o sonidos de la naturaleza, etc.

Si hubiera sonidos como en la app de Pomodoro Focus To-Do, siento que esta app resolvería mi vida. ¡Por favor, les suplico una actualización, ㅠㅡㅠㅡㅠ por favor!!!

### 일본어 (日本語):
すべて素晴らしいのですが、ポモドーロタイマーを使うときに音が鳴れば嬉しいです。

秒針の音、風の音、自然の音など。

Focus To-Doというポモドーロアプリのように音が鳴れば、このアプリだけで私の人生が解決できるような気がします。お願いです、アップデートをお願いします、ㅠㅡㅠㅡㅠお願い!!!

title: Streaks라 쓰고 “마누라”라고 부른다!
body:
혼자 사는 사람입니다. 
습관이 중요한 줄 알면서도
습관 들이는 게 어찌나 어렵던지요. 
쌓여가는 영양제, 불어나는 지방.. 
처음에는 호기롭게 계획을 세우고도 금새 그만두기를 반복했었는데, 이 앱을 통해 조금씩 생활이 잡히기 시작했습니다. 

물론, 중간에 앱을 지웠다 깐 적도 있습니다. 
몇 개월 동안 사용하지 않을 땐, 
이 앱이 꼭 족쇄처럼 느껴져서 쳐다보기도 싫었던 적도 있었지요. 
하지만, 다시 시작한 하루, 또 하루가 모여
어느새 늘어난 숫자들을 바라보며 
그만큼 변화된 자신을 발견하는 기쁨이 꽤 쏠쏠합니다. 

좋은 앱을 만들어 주심에 감사드리며,
이런 리뷰는 처음 남겨보는데, 
앱 설치를 망설이는 분들에게 조금이라도 도움이 되었으면 좋겠습니다.

(참고로 이 글은 어떠한 강요도 지원도 받지 않고 작성된 것임을 밝힙니다.)

title: Could be better
body:
First off I’d love to say how great this is, especially as someone who’s as forgetful as I am, and this is where it could be way better. As much as I think this app will help me it cannot satisfy my needs for number of tasks and it would be great if it could be more lenient for people who are forgetful, have ADHD etc. I have to write absolutely everything down to get things done and it would be nice if this could be considered. For me and my partner it is a let down to see because it would demotivate fully able people it therefore renders it partially useful for us and our needs. 

Other trackers haven’t worked well or been as easy to use, and the most effective we had was making our own on paper. But since our phones are always with us and it’s easier to track through phone like this it is way more beneficial for us to be able to put all the things we need to get done here.

I hope this can be a consideration at least to maybe allow for more or put it behind a mode to not deter people who tend to get unmotivated. 

Over all I’d love to applaud this app despite it being the first day in use, even though we have to supplement with something else.

title: A little masterpiece
body:
I absolutely love Streaks. It’s one of the few apps that I’ve stuck to and use multiple times a day. The concept is simple and easy to understand, the design is clean and clutter free and tracking habits is as pain free as it gets. So the app actually does what it promises: Helping you stick to good habits. 

A couple of nifty features I really appreciate: 
- Automatic tracking using Apple Health data: Yes!! No double tracking of things your phone already knows. Just read the data that’s already there. No action needed.
- Customizable color theme: Go black! Perfect if you open the app after lights out:  no bright screen hurting your eyes.
- The perfect Watch app: complication on the watch face for a quick view of your daily task completion progress. Tap it, tap the habit you just completed and boom, you’re done. Timed habits too - just start the timer and get to work on whatever it is you’re tracking. The task autocompletes when the timer is up. That’s it. Pain free. 
- Suggestions for adjusting habits that are too easy or too hard: Find it hard to get all those steps? The app suggests a lower target so you don’t give up. Nailing it on your workout duration? The app suggests taking it up a notch to go from good habits  to great habits.

Streaks developers - you absolutely crushed it with this one. Congratulations!

title: This app is weird.
body: Software engineer here. Can’t comprehend why does it requires background app refresh to display the timer across devices. Other apps with very similar design can get ahead without it. Sometimes I see a black screen and the countdown on Apple Watch while multitasking in the dock. If the UI drops, just render the countdown with task name or allow me to choose myself how do I want to see time left for timed task. Lack of Up Next view on Apple Watch is a massive turn off for me. I use four separate pages to group tasks by nature: physical, mind etc. The dots widget on AW isn’t dynamic so once a day task gets complete I cannot see a new one I can accomplish from a different page. For repetitive timed tasks: lack of notification repeat if frustrating. Let’s say I make squats 8 times per day each hour. The only way for me to get reminded is by manually entering times for each of those. Rather than following a more rational flow: get a notification -> squat -> countdown starts once the user taps the round is completed. I would say with the current functionality this app is worth around 50% of the asking price.

title: Simple, polished app.
body:
Streaks knows its purpose and does the job well. The interface is clean, there are no distractions, even when it asks for a review, it does so in an elegant way. I bought it in a bundle with Streaks Workout, which I absolutely adore. This is 'just' very good, so if you seem to like it, at least take a look at the other app.

Some notes on what's offered. You can choose up to six actions to track, every one can be attached to certain days. So I can track chess practice on fridays and wednesdays, and bodyweight workouts every day except Sunday. You only have to type the name of the activity, and the app tries to guess the icon for you. As soon as I have written Chess practice, a chess piece icon was attached. This is a good example of the attention to detail shown here.

All in all, a very good app. I will follow further offerings from this developer.

title: A real pleasure to use
body: This app is so AWESOME. Beautifully designed, incredibly easy to use and most important of all: actually works. There's something special about wanting to keep a streak that makes you want to do the desired task again and soon enough it becomes a habit. I would really love to have the option to add more than 6 tasks though. I've already ran out of available tasks. Let's say you want to measure your weight daily, drink at least 1,5l of water daily, workout 3 times a week, run twice a week, read a book on the weekends, study another language on week days. That's already 6 tasks and I'd like to add more. I understand that one of the strengths of Streaks is to keep it simple, but it simply isn't enough. I'd love to use Streaks not only as a "habit creating" app but also as a motivation to keep doing several other things and let's be honest: 6 tasks isn't even equal to the number of days in a week - maybe limit it to 6 tasks a day if you want to keep it simple? Bring it on, Streaks! Anyway, I highly recommend Streaks. :)

body:
I have been using the app for more than 2 years. As someone who has tried dozens of habit apps, I have found Streak to be the best of the bunch.

What I love most about Streak is the customisation options - I have never seen such thorough settings as here. You can chose from pre-set or create your new custom habit: changing times to do per day, timer with notifications, reminders, sounds, possibility to switch off apps badge - and it’s all can be different for any habit. The design is also simply beautiful. Love changing colors of pages from time to time. 

Guys, I think you would succeed in making a to-do list app even tho there are plenty of them but no as perfect as streak for habits.

title: Хорошо, но хотелось бы лучше
body:
Приложение неплохое, но есть много недоработок. 
Например,
1. Неадекватная работа уведомлений и подсчета. Когда надо не уведомляет и не сбрасывает счётчик (чистка зубов - выполнил 3 чистки, завтра уже можно не чистить, счётчик не сбросился, засчитать не даёт), когда не надо трезвонит безумолку (поставил же 2 раза в неделю, нет, на следующий день будет напоминать, вдруг я подряд захочу потренироваться). 
2. «Тренировка Streak» засчитывается, когда пользуемся приложением Workout. Но почему нельзя сделать дополнительную индивидуальную задачу с привязкой к Workout? Дублирую, переименовываю, делаю своё расписание и после выполнения в Workout оно засчитывается вместе с первым заданием, которое со вторым никак не связано. Сделаете 6 индивидуальных занятий на основе Workout - они засчитаются все разом вне расписания. Удивлён таким ограничением. 
3. Задача повторяющаяся несколько раз в день. Например, чистка зубов. Спасибо за то, что разрешили убрать ненужный мне таймер. Имеем 3 уведомления на время, но не имеет возможности указать 3 интервала активации значка приложения (только авто или 1 интервал). Какой? С 7:00 до 23:00? Не удобно.
4. Далее. Нигде нет описания настроек и визуализации. 
Что за «Кнопка действия»? Почему где-то доступно это действие (хронометраж/счёт), где-то просит вставить какую-то ссылку. Как Workout привязать хотя бы. Как сделать хронометраж? Выбрана тренировка Хоккей, 10:00 (дриблинг). Как подключить хронометраж??? Выбирать Чистка зубов с настроенным хронометражем и переименовывать на хоккей? Бред же. 

Настройки Apple Watch в приложении. Точки, графика, модули, огромный... Что!? Кто здесь? Кстати, иконки приложения на телефоне поменял на чёрные, в часах так и остались оранжевые. Не порядок. 

Управление данными - действия: это ещё что? Звучит интересно, а как пользоваться то?
В общем нужен подробный мануал с картинками, хотя бы на английском языке. 

Итого - хорошая задумка, но пока оно только про дизайн, а не функционал. Но потенциал есть, мне нравится, продолжу пользоваться.

body: Долго думал насчёт покупки, сомневался, пытался справиться встроенными или бесплатными сервисами. После разочаровался в этой идее, и просто купил. Честно - это лучшее приложения для статистических, временных, постоянных и любых заданий. Не список покупок, не планировщик на день - нет. Это лучшее приложения для напоминаний, отслеживании их выполнения. Лучшее, что в нем есть - это система конструктора - больше не нужны приложения для фитнеса, напоминания пить воду, подсчёт количества отжиманий, невыкуренных сигарет, сколько времени ты писал диплом, и вообще всего, что можно посчитать числами или временем. Пока не заметил ни одного минуса, ни единого. Если что - дополню, пока что крайне уверенная рекомендация

UPD. Спустя пару недель чуть привык. Задачи с кофе теперь на оборотной стороне, и они не мозолят глаз. Как раз задачи с «не...» лучше всего держать там. Но теперь мозолят глаз следующие 2 вещи: фон виджета (хотелось бы прозрачный как у всех нормальных приложений) и цвета (после использования color picker в pro версии Focus Keeper пресеты кажутся прям ленивым решением со стороны разработчика).

title: Не мотивирует
body: Да у приложения отличный дизайн, все грамотно оформлено в плане UX. Но как оказалось с задачей своей оно вообще не справляется... увы. Да можно добавить кучу задач/привычек. Которые нужно выполнять раз в день или неделю или два раза в день. Но суть в том, что если ты выполнишь задачу 100 или 1000 раз подряд или не выполнишь ее столько же раз ничего не будет. Вообще... ничего. Т.е. один раз пропустил задачу и просто смахнул уведомление... и все. Ничего не будет. Таким образом программа это просто трекер уже сложившихся привычек и ничего более. Новые привычки она вам не поможет выработать и уж тем более бросить курить!!! Пол года пользовался, потом понял что просто разницы никакой нет. Все что делал исправно раньше и продолжил делать, все новые привычки, не прижились за пол года. А значит программ не выполняет свою задачу. Нужна система наград чтоли или мини целей...

body:
Самое классное приложение из подобных, позволяет ставить задачи на каждый день как позитивные (не забыть выгулять собаку), так и помогает вырабатывать привычку от чего-то отказаться (например, от курения). Можно устанавливать напоминания, следить за прогрессом, ставить любые иконки (коих много), соответствующие задачам. Приятная плюшка - изменение цвета экрана на свой вкус. 

Благодаря приложению можно не думать о том, что сегодня нужно сделать. Оно напомнит вам само!

title: Not worth the money
body: Does what it says on tin, but in a rather awkward way. UI does not follow normal conventions; and sadly not in a way that makes the app more convenient once you learn how to use it. While it syncs status of your tasks, it will not sync your notification settings. Combined with a default of notifying/reminding at random times (why?) rather than defaulting to no reminder you are forced to remove reminders on all your devices every time you add a task to avoid getting reminders all day. The app reminds me of 90s where a lot of software was written by amateurs with little UI design experience and where doing your own thing with the hope of perhaps making the UI much easier to use (it never was) was still acceptable. That said, the app does what it claims to do and I love that it is a one time purchase. Just not worth the money

body:
I’ve only used it for three days so far so I can’t speak for long term usage. But so far I’m really impressed. It’s really clean and simple, good integration with Apple Health, excellent to be able to use shortcuts as actions. The widget is also extremely good, and that’s perhaps the most important thing, to get a good reminder each time I unlock my phone.
All the other habit trackers I’ve used so far I’ve given up on almost right away. This one has kept me going for three days, which is a new record.
I’ll revise my review after a few months if I continue to use it and what I think about it. Perhaps it will earn a 5 star.
But so far so good!

title: Great app but implementation of “Gold Theme” feature not ideal
body:
I feel that the implementation of the “show a gold theme for the remainder of a successful  day” feature Is not ideal. 

First of all, why must I have 6 habits for the gold theme to work? Everybody have different number of goals that they want to achieve. The theme should turn to gold even if I only have 1 habit in my list and I have completed this one single habit for the day. 

Also, if I have total of 7 habits that I need to accomplish for the day, the icons shouldn’t turn to gold after completing 6 of them. 

The icons should only turn to gold after I have completed all the habits that I have set up for the day. 

Other than this, I have to say that this is a really great habit tracking app. There is an unexplainable sense of achievement from long pressing the icon to mark the task as complete. Simple yet effective.

This app really helps give me the push that I needed as this game system of 'streaks' and the periodical daily reminder nagging helps me to take action! This app won't miraculously help your productivity, as it requires the user to already have the will to enforce positive habit.  However this app does helps give you the final push in a visual format and the sense of accomplishment when finishing a task. Great app!

title: Most well designed habit tracker
body:
Actually understands how to get you to stick and not stick to a habit.  The limit to the amount of habits you can track is a good thing.  The integration with health is smart.  One of my favorite features are the smart notifications that learns your behavior and the ability to set the period of time of when an unfinished habit appears as a badge notification so that habits you can no longer achieve that day isn't on the app all day.

Overall, very smartly designed in terms of what to put in and what not to.

My only frustration is the inability to set a health habit to automatically track the time I wake up.  Right now you can only track the length of sleep.  Thought this would be a common habiy.  ;)

Thanks for making this app to help us be better versions ofnourselves!

title: Feedback on Streaks for Mac
body:
I’ve been a happy Streaks user on iOS, so I was excited to see a Mac version. While the app works and syncs well, there are a few areas that could improve the Mac experience:
	1.	The menubar icon opens a separate, resizable window instead of an integrated pop-up. It feels less polished compared to other menubar apps.
	2.	There’s no option to launch the app at startup, which is essential for habit tracking.
	3.	The window resizing feels unnecessary for a menubar app; a fixed size would be more user-friendly.

Streaks is a great app, but I hope the Mac version gets updates to better suit the platform. I’d love to see these adjustments in future releases!

title: 很好，但是改進會更優
body:
優點：

3、與健康程式配對，不用一定要按，透過手錶可以讀取，運動以及站立時間…等等。

缺點：
1、只能標定六項目標！
2、無法在其他方面，例如喝水、健身等等，例如目標是2000，今天只做了1500，則是無法標注在上面，形成完成度！

建議：
大目標下面可以分割幾個小目標，這樣，不僅可以幫助檢視，還可以觀察進度，讓使用者更好達到目標！

title: Simple, yet powerful. Perfect for writing goals
body: I had one very specific use for this app. I am an aspiring writer and I needed a way to motivate myself to get in the habit of writing regularly. This app is PERFECT for that. I have a goal to write for 30 min 6 days a week. I love that I can set a timer right from the app. It is absolutely critical that they have a watch app too because my phone is often my source of distraction so being able to toggle things from my watch is perfect. I love that this is NOT A SUBSCRIPTION. Absolutely worth the one time cost. One of thing that is great is if you’ve been tracking with something else before this, you can retroactively add that data to the app so you don’t have to start from scratch. I’ve already written for more consecutive days using this app that I’ve managed in the last 6 months. I highly recommend.

I love how the app syncs with other Apple apps. Very intuitive. 

It’s also a simple clean design! As others have said, very customizable.

My suggestions: 
1. A to-do list feature. I know the app is all about streaks (duh), but it’d be nice to have all the things I need to do in one place. Having a page for one-time tasks you can check off would be awesome. 

2. There’s a bit of a learning curve in the beginning. The help page has everything you need to know, but maybe a lengthier tutorial in the beginning would help people jump in quicker.

title: Is this the missing key??
body: Wasn’t sure what to expect from Streaks. Sure, it has high ratings and a simple, clean interface- but how does it hold up against my stubborn ways? Well, I’m here to say so far it holds up extremely well! Has it only been one day of usage? Sure, but I’ve gotten more accomplished in that day than I have in the past week. Streaks seems to hit that perfect balance between simplicity and functionality. Many of the tasks can be automatically tracked/completed by syncing with your phone’s data, which has proved to be very handy since I don’t like having to manually track tasks. I adore all the customization features and various widgets that are available. The Apple Watch app is fantastic too, as you can easily keep an eye on/mark off tasks as you go about your day. My only improvement would be that I wish the watch app allowed you to view only uncompleted and upcoming tasks at the touch of a button, like is possible on the phone app. Other than that and possibly adding in even more customization features, it’s a truly great app that I hope continues to motivate me to better myself every day!

title: Why only 24 habits?
body:
This is a good app and I’ve been using it for a long time but I don’t understand why after years of updating the app the developers voluntarily limit the number of habits to 24. That gives competitor apps an edge that could easily be corrected. I personally ended up using more other tracking apps than this one because of this limit, even though this is a great app. Some of us manage more tasks and want to track more data, for example for business, not only personal tasks. Another thing is that there’s very few apps that offer team habit completion for partners or couples (mostly focused on house chores), this app could easily get an edge on that market too since it offers habit sharing. But the problem is that 24 habit limit interface design that in my opinion is more arbitrary (maybe trying to keep it simple) than profitable. More habits does not mean less simplicity. Simplicity is achieved through the interface design, not through limiting the number of data.
Also it would be nice to let mark habits as completed from the widget and not having to open the app all the time. Please consider these suggestions. It’s a good app but it could still be improved. Thank you

title: Most Life Changing App Ever!

I’ve been more consistent about doing things like practicing the guitar, reading, working out, stretching and even using the negative task feature to stop myself from playing phone games (which I can be helplessly addicted too).  I have recommended this app to so many people already and if you’re reading this take it as a sign to get it for yourself! title: Keeping it simple…. While having powerful features
body:
A great app if you are trying  to reinforce some changes.

On the surface, this app is simple and super easy to use (like lots of similar apps).  Dive a bit dealer and you find JUST ENOUGH advanced features to make the app more useful when you want.  A favorite feature = the simple prompt to check off a habit yesterday.  It is going to happen that, 1 day ago, you DID do that thing… you just did not check it off at that moment.  A subtitle reminder to stay focused and track your progress.  

The organization of “pages” of habits allows me to create a morning routine that is visually separate from evening or those habits not connected to a time of day.  And I can have habits that are weekly (or multiple times per week) on a separate “page”.

But it should be easy to track habit completion as the app works on every Apple device I own…phone, iPad, watch and Mac.  Syncing coul be a little faster but eventually it does get “current”.

title: Very Unpolished for Paid App
body:
This app would be acceptable if it were free, but for a paid app, I expect more. 

1) Setting up notifications is difficult and requires a separate step outside of setting up the task. The notifications should be able to be set up per sub task. It would be better if you could edit a task and set a notification time for each sub task. 
2) Notifications are not reliable on Apple Watch. I only get a 2 notifications per day on a task with 5 sub tasks. 
3) If I complete all sub tasks early in the day, I still get notifications later in the day. Having the ability to add a notification time per sub task might help solve this as the notifications would not be completely separate from the tasks themselves. 
4) I can’t figure out how to edit a future task. I can only edit tasks that are scheduled for the current day. 

I love the idea of this app but it is missing a huge amount of polish.

title: Get This App – also a suggestion!
body:

When I first used this app I added too many tasks, got overwhelmed, didn’t want to open it cause it was too much, than stopped using it after a month…

I picked it back up again and kept it simple. Over the past year it has developed into an essential tool for my day. Just 6 streaks. The customization and flexibility is great. Especially with notifications, badge icons, and SHORTCUT INTEGRATION. I am reading, working out, watching less YouTube and learning more as a result. Daily small changes and improvements in my life. Keep is small and build on those habits! I love being able to comment on different complete actions and track the stats.

Improvement suggestion: When you assign an ‘Action Button’ to ‘Incomplete Task’ you can only choose/check one action… This means that if you have a timed task, and want to start the timer and have it run a shortcut you can’t do both. It would be great if I could launch a shortcut and have it start the timer in the app!

Thanks if you read this far! Keep up the work. Worth every penny.

I recommend Streaks study the data about how many people actually pick up habits consistently again after breaking a very long streak.

Maybe there can be some sort of redemption mechanic. Perhaps a gold-day can allow someone to resume their past streak of 1-2 lapsed items? Just a suggestion, as I really appreciate having an app like Streaks to help me form and keep to my habits but find it all too easy to break down into dysfunction after just one "bad day."

Alas for me, I constantly close background apps in a quest for decent battery life and reduced visual clutter, and if Streaks is not open, the shortcut will fail to log activity into Streaks 100% of the time. Shortcuts are able to create entries in other apps without them being perpetually open and 3. Shortcuts has steps like “open app” available for programming, which would solve my main issue, except Streaks isn’t an option there.

Glad this app is an one time purchase vs constant subscription fees, but it doesn’t meet my needs for the singular, explicit function I bought it for. I think it’s a good app, just not for me (yet.) title: Great except for bizarre sync issues
body:
Overall a great idea and well executed except for the iCloud sync behavior. It's honestly beyond me how the sync in this app works. I'll often complete a task and then it will immediately uncomplete itself and the maybe come back shortly after. This should never happen if sync was implemented in a sane way, where each device records immutable events with timestamps and you just apply them in order. Once I've completed a task that event should be recorded and I should never see a state where the task is not complete unless I explicitly undo the completion (which itself is another event and applied in the right order based on timestamps should not cause any problems). But I constantly get into states where tasks I completed on the current device mysteriously show up as not completed anymore and maybe correct themselves later. Or not.

I use this app across iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch which makes the sync issues rather obnoxious. It does seem like it's gotten "better" but this isn't something that should get incrementally better, they should just fix their sync design and all the issues would go away permanently.

title: It Knows You Better Than You Think You Know Yourself
body:

I've used Notion, Habitify, and Habitica for weeks and months at a time and always come back to Streaks. Although Streaks is not objectively the most robust or feature-rich solution, that's exactly why it's the best - especially the 24 habit cap. For me I would enevitably end up creating more habits than I could realistically accomplish each day with the other apps. But with Streaks they forced me to think more critically on the most important 24 habits I wanted to form a streak with. I've found that actually being able to complete your habits is FAR more motivating than simply having every concievable habit in your app. And finally, dividing the 24 habits into four pages might seem awkward at first but it turns out that by segmenting your day into four sections it's actaully more exciting and motivating to complete each page thus giving you more sustained motivation throughout the day - who knew!? All that being said the app is top-notch quality and the fact that I can use on my mac, phone, and watch really does make this the best habit tracking app....for apple users!

title: Transformative & Seamless: Streaks - A Cornerstone of My Fitness Journey
body:
As someone deeply invested in fitness and technology, I'm often on the lookout for apps that not only promise results but actually deliver them. Streaks is one such gem. It has been an integral part of my daily routine, contributing significantly to my achievement of a 1,368-day workout streak. This journey of mine even caught the attention of Men's Health, a testament to the efficacy of the habits Streaks helped me cultivate.

What sets Streaks apart is its simplicity and focus. It's not just another task manager; it's a lifestyle enhancer. The app's intuitive design, available on both iPhone and Apple Watch, makes tracking daily goals effortless and engaging. Its ability to sync seamlessly with Apple Health is a game-changer. This integration means that data from various workouts and health apps I use are automatically imported into Streaks. Why is this important? It provides a holistic view of my fitness regimen without the hassle of manual entries. The convenience of having all my health data consolidated in one place cannot be overstated. It allows for a more comprehensive understanding of my fitness progress and patterns.

Another aspect worth noting is how Streaks leverages the psychology of habit formation. The app doesn't just track your habits; it encourages and motivates you to maintain them. The satisfaction of maintaining a streak is a powerful motivator, and Streaks capitalizes on this brilliantly. For me, seeing my workout streak grow day by day was not just motivational but also a source of personal pride.

I first stumbled upon Streaks through a blog post by Matt Mullenweg, founder and CEO of Automattic/WordPress. His recommendation spoke volumes, and the app has lived up to every bit of the promise. Whether you're looking to start a new habit or maintain an existing one, Streaks is the perfect companion.

Streaks stands out as one of the most useful apps on my iPhone and Apple Watch. It is more than just an app; it is a daily partner in my journey towards sustained health and wellness. For anyone looking to embark on or maintain a health journey, I cannot recommend Streaks highly enough. It is a prime example of how technology can be harnessed to improve our daily lives in meaningful ways.

title: Life-changing but with a lot more room for improvement
body:
I started using Streaks as a part of my depression combating plan. I needed an app to remind me of the basics of life such as taking a shower, taking vitamins and meds, housekeeping, tracking weight, working out, sleeping on time, drinking water, brushing teeth, enjoying a cup of coffee, reading a book, writing a journal, ..., etc.
It has dramatically changed my life in just a couple of weeks. I don't really care about doing streaks, but I desperately needed reminders and a way to keep track of things.

== What I Like ==
- Integrates well with iOS, WatchOS, MacOS, Apple Health, Apple Shortcuts, and widgets
- You can connect "start actions" to Apple shortcuts, which I absolutely love, since I turn related "Focus" modes on (but I can't turn it off, see below)
- It allows you to export your data as CSV
- Many options for theming

== Needs Improvement ==
- The UI/UX is an absolute nightmare. It's not intuitive at all. You find what you're looking for if you're lucky. There are surprising elements, random icons, and random numbers all over the place and you have to press everything randomly like a monkey to discover features. It's like they forced themselves to be in a certain visual language/framework, and they lost all sense of common sense. I had (and sometimes still have) a very hard time understanding why I have different sections, what is the icon on top for, how to reorder things when labels are not visible, why does some tasks don't allow me to change the task type and some other properties, what does it mean when I set my Task Days to 1 day a week, and there's a setting right below saying 1 time/day? What does the numbers at the bottom mean? Why is the stats icon a star, which commonly means "favorite" in the industry? What does "upcoming" task even mean, I have 24 habits and I they don't need to follow a specific order, I just need to make sure I do them. The litmus test for good design is "do they need a manual for this"? And you ABSOLUTELY need the manual for more than half of the features.
- Stats are only limited to the page you're viewing, I need an overall view (again, why do we have pages?). Also you can't view the actual values on the graph, which renders them useless, you're just looking at random bumps... What does the "time graph" even mean? Is it an average of every day? 
- Limits you to only a maximum of 24 habits. I already filled it up and can't add more...
- App timers are not syncing across devices unless you stop it on one and refresh it on the other, and sometimes it doesn't work at all
- You can't connect a shortcut to a "timer stopped" action for timers. This is really bad because I can't turn off my Focus mode automatically when the timer is done
- When you connect a shortcut, it opens the Shortcuts App every time the action is triggered, which is really annoying
- Multiple timers can be started together, which is pretty bad since I want other timers to stop when I start a different timer. Sometimes I forget to stop the other timers and it skews the data
- Data exports don't contain your Apple Health stats
- There's no RPC APIs (just callback URLs) I can use to integrate my habits or stats with my Obsidian notes

Pretty sure I forgot many other annoyances I have, but all these improvements are listed simply because I love the app and I can see the potential if the gaps are filled. Many thanks to all the people involved in making this app, and I truly hope to see the app in a better place soon.

title: CHANGED MY LIFE IN 40 DAYS - MUST HAVE APP
body:
I have been wanting an app like this for years. A fellow self help junkie friend of mine told me about this app & at first I was reticent to want to buy it, but I trusted him so I did & wow! Best $4.99 I may have ever spent! 

I am not 40+ days into using it & I have limited my social media to 30 minutes to 1 hour a day, I’m more productive & focused for sure, I have started writing my book & I’m tracking my writing progress, and I have gotten several other people to get the app as well. I finally have the right tool that’s fun & easy to use to keep me on track with my own goals! 

I have tried other free habits apps & there is nothing like Streaks out there. This is literally a dreams come true. I only wish there was a goals at a glance page for my 6 daily goals, 90 day goals, my monthly goals, & my yearly goals. Maybe they can make that next! I also wish I could have 6 more streaks goals. I feel like I need 1 more page or at least an option for more pages. Not because I do every streak goal every day, but seeing my overall goals everyday keeps me motivated and focused! 

I separated my streaks pages into 4 categories: 

Page 1: My Morning Routine (Bible, prayer, write my ten 90 day goals, read 10 pages or 20 minutes, write my 6 goals for the day..) 
Page 2: My Health / Day Routine including listening to motivational audio (often while I work out), 72 oz water, get ready for the day) 
Page 3: My Work Habits (work 30 min on my business, Read 30 min to 1 hour in my industry to join the top 10%, plan, film or edit a YouTube video..) 
Page 4: My night routine (putting the kitchen to bed, checking screen time to see if I made my 30 min - 1 hour social media goal, clean my face, bedtime..) 

Thank you Streaks! I hope this doesn’t become a subscription because currently it’s the best thing ever. I will be making a YouTube video about this app at YouTube.com/CamilleHarris

body: I am a psychologist and I have worked with a lot of people who want to improve their organizational skills and executive functions (particularly those with ADHD) and I have recommended a lot of to do list type programs to people who have mixed success. This program is different. It helps you focus on a small amount of recurring tasks (it’s not for reminding you to send your aunt a thank you card). It is simple and rewarding to use, particularly with Apple Watch. The ability to customize the icons is fun and makes the tasks feel more like they are part of you. title: Great, but I miss the interactive Today Screen widget
body:

It was a HUGE game changer to be able to complete tasks without even having to open the app (pressing on a task within the widget would allow you to mark that task as complete). Now, the current widget options only allow you to see task progress; you cannot actually interact with the widget (pressing the widget will only open the app). 

PLEASE please please, if any of the app developers are reading this, will you add the interactive widget back!!! 🙏🙏🙏 I know this is a small, almost nit-picky request, but it has *completely* changed the experience and efficacy of the app for myself and, I am sure, many others. title: Great; gripes are in the minutiae
body:
Ok this app is getting 5 stars because it is simple and straightforward. Well featured and robust details without too much clutter. I like it a lot and have been using it very well.

My minor gripe is that the apple watch app has slightly different controls, and I develop conflicting user habits since I use both mobile and watch apps every day. For example the watch app scrolls up and down to change pages (which I actually like better!) while the mobile app changes pages by horizontal flipping of cards. Same with click to complete vs. press and hold to complete.
Very minor details but since I’m doing them so often, it is burdensome to get confused trying to quickly complete tasks. For example, accidentally clicking instead of press and holding on a task to complete it in the mobile app will cycle the task view to the calendar and subsequent options. One misclick can have you cycle through 3-4 alternate task views before you can return to the normal one and complete the task, turning a 2-second interaction into a 5-second one. Again, it adds up, which is why I am here writing this.

I would prefer to just do a better job automating completions to avoid having to click to complete tasks in the first place, but the shortcuts app has limited options.

title: A Good App that Keeps Getting Better
body:
I used to use this app a lot back in 2009 when it was a free app, and in its infancy. When the phone I was using back then died, I forgot to reinstall it. 

I went on about my life, relying on my calendar and memo and list-making apps, and setting a million different alarms on my phone. 

While those systems have all worked well for me, I found myself, recently, wanting to know at a glance how often I was doing certain things, and I remembered how much I had liked using this app. 

I looked it up, saw that the developers had made some changes that appealed to me, and that it is now a paid app. 

I feel it is not too expensive for something that solidly and consistently helps *me* to be more solid and consistent in the ways I show up in my life. I’m glad to see the ways that it has become a stronger app since the last time I used it regularly. I like it a lot.

title: Encourage the Hesistant to Try
body:
I definitely fall into the camp of too lazy to write reviews, even when they are well-deserved. When the pop-up came up to rate the Streaks app, I felt compelled mostly thinking of the next person who might benefit. 

This app offers a lot so that you can really customize your experience. It has taken into account that not all goals or parameters of success are measured the same and even allows you to differentiate between the "do" goals vs. the "do not" goals (i.e. do drink 100 oz of water/day, do not drink alcohol). I know there are a lot of ways I am underutilizing this app. I think this is mostly due to the lack of instructions especially the app on your phone vs the one on my computer/Mac. 

The biggest benefit I have found is that the interface (like grouping like goals) has resulted in internal motivation. When I complete one goal, visually seeing it completed and the ones next to it not completed, tricks my mind into wanting to complete the other goals simply to check them off the list. 

One complaint I do have is not being able to (or not knowing how) to rearrange goals on different pages after they are created and I have been tracking them for a while. For example, I have a goal to journal every day and to study art for X amount of time/day. Originally, these generally seemed like they fell into a similar category; however, I recently created additional art goals like drawing 50 circles/day, drawing 50 ovals/day, etc. etc. I would like to move the journal every day on a separate page but have not figured it out and do not want to lose what I have captured by simply restarting.

title: Falling prey to adding complexity for the sake of complexity
body:
Full disclosure, I’m an experience designer but I’ve tried to separate the “academic” from my experience of the app. 

I’ve used Streaks on and off for years. I came back to it in late 2022 and my overall thought is that “less is more” has fallen a little by the wayside. For example, could you please make it “fall off a log” easy to have a view that shows all one’s tasks regardless of positive/negative/completion status?

I understand why some may want the level of filtering / number of views but honestly, I really just need to see all tasks with all statuses - and I’d bet I’m not alone. This also could increase retention with new users. Thanks!

Nice to have: a tally-like option to simply count when you did something, with no specific date or number requirements. Use case: days I went on a road trip, days I went to Target, days I went to the beach.

title: Outstanding habit-building support
body:
I love the Steaks app. It is simple enough to get started right away, persistent enough to get my attention when I have a spare moment, subtle enough that it doesn’t draw my attention away when I’m busy, and nicely designed. 

I really enjoy using the app and I find that my thinking has shifted substantially since I started using it. I entered a goal for “eat a healthy meal” and while that might seem utterly underwhelming as my target is literally *one* healthy meal at some point during the day. My focus has shifted from “what am I going to eat for lunch?” when my work schedule gets too crazy for what I had planned, to “what healthy meal will I eat today?” This has the knock on effect of generating loads of healthy meal ideas that I’m enthused about, without any real pressure. So my eating is better throughout the day. I was eating fast food at least 3x/week before. I got fast food once in the last two weeks. Not perfect, but definitely progress I’m happy with.

I’ve set similarly effective goals for quality time with my kids, maintaining other relationships, and exercise. Some goals I don’t hit everyday, but I’m making progress on those too.

So glad I got this app. Best $5 I’ve spent in a long time.

title: The best—and no subscription BUT AVOID MAC VERSION
body:
UPDATE 2022-11-26: I made major changes to my habits—changing some existing ones and added new ones on my phone—his morning. I hadn't used my MacBook in a few days, and after using it I realized that instead of syncing all of my latest changes from my phone to my MBP, Streaks did the opposite and replaced all the work I'd done today with the days-old versions from my Mac. I'm still leaving my 5 star rave review on the iOS app store because I really like Streaks, but I've already deleted the app from my Mac.  

REQUEST: Please allow longer task labels—I often struggle to abbreviate them!  

REVIEW: Streaks does the job with style and flair. Love the design, and once you figure out how the settings work, it’s very easy to use. (If you don’t like the orange, it’s simple to change the colors of the interface and the icon.) The ability to archive habits is a nice touch, so if you decide to start one up again in the future, you don’t have to begin from scratch. I mostly use Streaks on my phone, but it’s nice having it on my Mac, too, where I leave it running mostly as a reminder and for when I’m working and leave my phone out of reach. I’ll never pay a recurring subscription to use a habit app. Fortunately, the best one in the App Store doesn’t require one.

title: Best routine/ habit building app out there
body:
Tried most of the popular routine/habits app out there. This is by far the smartest build, best design language and amazingly customizable one out there.

The four pages are very clean and is a direct interface for me to set my routines. So even though this app isn’t technically a routines app, it exceeds all my expectations for my needs. Especially love that it’s not a standard routine app where you have to do each task in a designated order or timeline (not always practical in day to day life, since everyday really varies ). I like that kind of flexibility.

Being able to easily “program ” the data you want to draw from the health app is a big plus, even the features that’s really hard to find in apple’s own software can easily be implemented in this app. For example, I want to weigh myself and record it to my health app everyday. It would be at least three or four clicks in the health app, and a bunch of scrolling. But if I link the data in one of my streak tasks, I can record it in steak, and that data will be saved in the health app with a single tap. I also like to sync my meditation time, workout time and steps between apps. Just the perfect presentation.

Also big thumbs up for the UI design. It gives me a geeky vibe, yet so simplistic it almost feels like a built in app. Same thing with the streak Apple Watch app, very pretty and great widgets for my watch face. Didn’t see any close competition in the other apps.

Finally, I like that it’s a one time purchase but not a subscription, and no stupid in app purchases. There are some out there that makes you pay for the icons, or just expensive subscription that does not give you that amount of value.

Great app. Hope more people use it.

title: Really Helpful   My Tips
body:
I've used a ton of little "make good habits" apps in the past and i rarely stick with anything, but this one has been great and is about as clean as it gets. I think a lot of them are bogged down by complexity or trying to do too much.

Tips for being successful with this from the time that I have used it:
• Fewer goals of higher import > many goals for everything you want to improve
• Make it a home screen widget
• Start your day with the app and think about what you should do to hit all the goals *before* other stuff
• Set *really* simple goals/habits and only increase them when you feel you've internalized the more basic version.

Lvo the app, only request is the ability to turn off/remove additional pages if you aren't using them.

title: Love it! But please add more habits.
body:
I bought this app years ago and true to my super ADHD self, I never used it- but I was at that point where something had to give for me, so I started playing with it and once I saw how customizable it was (while still staying relatively simple)- I was hooked. 
The only thing is, I would really love the option to have more habits. Between personal life and work life and social life - taking medications and breaking different tasks down, it would just be really nice to have that. 
I have found myself flipping through my boards all day, and it was right on my home dock thing on my phone- 
Also if there were more options to customize the icons- that would be great. There is a good mix there already, for sure- I would just love more. 

But thank you for making something that is so fool proof, even I can use it and stick with it 🤍
Already my mental health has started feeling so much better, and although I am a habitual procrastinator, I have found myself waking up early just so I can start ticking things off and getting that boost of serotonin from getting things accomplished 🤍 

But again… if we could get … two… or four 😅 more boards added- that would be so wonderful. I especially would like to break them up so for example I could arrange a board with my morning habits and one with my pm habits and one with my work habits, one with my mindful habits, a board for how I want to pay things off, a board for socialization (because I have to force myself, outside of work, to socialize, but since I’ve literally created daily and tasks for this… it’s really helping).. and perhaps one for physical exercise and different things I want to accomplish. 
Ps- I even added flossing, so my dentist will stop harassing me.. so thanks for that!

title: Great Servant, but a Terrible Master
body:
Let's get to the great part about this app.  I selected a bunch of things that were important to me, and added them to Streaks to follow through on them.  I went from thinking about them to touching my bases on them to get a streak going to getting things done at a regular time during my day.  I'm doing a lot better overall because of it.  I'm following through more and more on things that are important to me. 

So, why would I downgrade it one star?  It seems to have machine learned when I do things and has become more diligent at trying to remind me to do the things, as I'm doing them, breaking my zen far more often than I like.  Today, I was using a meditation app, and Streaks made a loud notification sound, disrupting my meditation, to tell me to meditate.  You can guess what that did. 

TLDR: Great app that will make you a better person, but turn off the notification sounds on each behavior you want to follow as you get better at your habits.

title: ADHD WINNER
body:
This app has changed my life and helped me overcome perfectionism when trying to build healthy habits while having ADHD. The customizations are great. THANK YOU!

On the flip side, I’m able to set off timed tasks that DO remind me when I haven’t done them (like take your meds, then eat half an hour later). 
All of this syncs to my apple watch, so I don’t have to remember to go write down that I did a thing.
I can then check my progress overall whenever I’m in a good place mentally to not beat myself up about things I missed - the easy to read UI lets me look at past months on my phone. 
Guess who’s taking her meds, using mouthwash, and applying acne cream more regularly over a 5 month period? (Hint - it’s me).

title: For the Medically Challenged
body:
I never leave reviews.  Ever.  But this app has helped change my life.  I'm 37, have extreme ADHD, was raised with a lot of support, and I've tried all the apps, but have never been able to form some of the simplest (good) habits.

Streaks is simple, clear (to this structurally/pattern/association oriented adhd brain), easy to stick with, and won't clutter up your task lists.

I am also a retired AAA games platform/software quality control and software engineer.  I can say this app is being developed by developers who take pride in their work, use their app, and understand how it needs to be used.  It is not only pretty but I love the UI.  It is functional and easy on the mind.  You can learn a few things quickly and as someone with memory issues, encapsulating each task and the reporting access on each node is fantastic and intuitive.

I look forward to new iterations and that is as someone who was a part of rapid release cycles (not that they churn you, just speaking from my perspective) who knows what that can do to the product and customers without top notch values around your users...I can honestly say, great job.

Some little snippets of their attention to detail:  using the wheel of your habit/task node to actively show you visual progress of a timed task.

The need for positively oriented vs negatively oriented habits (don't do this, do do this).  Flexibility in how you can count tasks (number of times over a period, for instance which might be good for a task like brushing a dog) that really reflect low friction ways of how people actually get things done.  This reduces stress from an unnecessarily rigid structure and frees up focus and time from fiddling with the system (like rescheduling).

They allow you to pause tasks as well.  I use this when I'm, say, out of town and it doesn't matter if I remember to water my plants.

I only wish, as someone with a need for more ongoing support in a number of tasks that the mobile version supported unlimited sheets.  I did get them to add some to the desktop version, but then it syncs to my phone and I have no way of accessing the extra sheets to mark things even though I'm getting alerts for them.  Oops!

I understand their philosophy in not focusing on building too many habits at once, but not everyone is working with the same needs or using this to just build habits with a neurotypical makeup.  So I use it differently.

title: Nice and Easy with a few missing features
body:
I just started using the app and I love it! It’s so simple to use, whether you’re adding/modifying tasks or adding new ones. However, there are just a few improvements I’d recommend. 

First, I have trouble holding myself accountable, and it really helps when others hold me accountable too. I see that there are sharing features, but it looks like I have to share the tasks one-at-a-time. I’d love to see an option where I can share all my boards with people and they can see all my stuff right away. 

Second, it looks like I can only add a maximum of 6 tasks per page? I’m not sure why that is. I guess it helps to see things at a glance and not have to scroll, but, especially on the iPad app, the icons are enormous, and it’d be nice to be able to add more than 6, scale down in size, and still all be visible at a glance. 

Otherwise, great app! Looking forward to seeing what features the future brings.

author: Lemonade from Lemons

title: Great but UI could be better
body:
Been using this app for 4 or 5 days now and I really love it but the UI is frustrating at times. I keep forgetting how to edit the tasks because the gear icon in the lower left corner suggests “settings” to me. My instinct is to long press the task itself to edit it but, of course, that triggers the task to be marked as done. As a result I wish there was a way to unmark tasks as done. Also, the wording of the notifications feels negative to me. Instead of being reminded to not break the streak, how about encouraging us to keep the streak going? Something like: “You’ve done this task 5 in a row—make it 6! You can do it!” The 10% Percent Happier app celebrates streaks by letting users share a graphic on social media so we can show our pride in keeping our meditation streak going. That would be a cool thing to add to this app! If it weren’t for the “streak” option on the 10% Happier app I’d not have bought this app. I realize now that I have a really powerful completist urge in me. What if you added a “custom reminder message” option? Or allow for an option for both “if you fail” messages and “you can succeed” messages? These “if you fail” messages are really getting me down. I want to believe I can succeed, not live in fear of failing.

UPDATE: So there is a limit of 12 tasks. This seems kind of nuts. Considering you can have the app track daily and WEEKLY tasks, how is 12 tasks enough? I have several things I do daily and several more things I do multiple times a week but not every day. The help page basically explains that only 12 tasks is for your own good, but I wish the devs would treat users with enough respect to let us decide how many tasks we can handle. Dropped a star because you think you’re protecting me but you’re actually holding me back.
author: Nerdy Pete

title: Great app! Feature Request

I’m finding I’m (insert bad habit here) more often than X times a day and it varies. I’d rather keep tabs on it with a counter than say “whelp I missed it X times today”, forget about it, and not record any more data.

title: Its a great app.
body:
Couple things have been bothering me though. One is the teeth brushing tracker. I have one of those fancy toothbrushes that will connect with the health app to track my usage. Its probably completely useless… but my issue is that in streaks it will count it automatically based on time, not instance. Using the brush’s app, I brush based on the motion tracker and all sorts of things so theres no exact time a “good” brushing will be done. So in the streaks app, it will consider the task incomplete if say, its under 3 mins, or it will say both times I do it are complete if its set to say, one minute. That shouldn't be. Two times a day should mean two instances… not 4 minutes or 2 minutes total or whatever. Alternatively, if I switch to tongue cleaning right after which takes only 30 seconds, the app only registers that time stamp instead of the brushing session before it… so i have to go in and just manually finish off the instance which defeats the purpose of having it connected to the health app to do it automatically anyways. 

So yeah not the end of the world, but I figure if this app is going to be offering these kinds of things maybe just tweak it so it does it right. Maybe just offer the ability to not base it off of time but just how many times. 

The other thing that has been bothering me is the color scheme. The options are all of these very bold and yucky colors. I mean… again not super important but maybe look into what colors are trending like from pantone or something… you’ll attract more customers I’m sure from just using color psychology like that. I believe lately pastels have been pretty popular, just as a tip.

body:
First of all this app is overall fantastic. I’ve been using it daily to keep myself on task with so many goals and habits, from drinking water to practicing my second language, meditating, exercising, reducing alcohol and even going to bed earlier. The devs have done such a great job. Thank you for an awesome app!

Having said that there are a few things I notice that make the app a bit less useful than it could be for me, and sometimes downright annoying:
1. Bonus time/counts — we NEED to be able to track when we go above and beyond our goal for a task! If I reach my 10 glasses of water/day and get in 2 more I wanna record that! If I hit my 6 hours for waist training and squeeze out another hour I want that credit!
Think of how well this could play into weekly/monthly goals. Maybe one day I can only do 5 hours but another I can do 7. I’m still on track for a weekly target but presently if I don’t hit exactly 6 every day I’ve effectively accomplished nothing. Not awesome. Right now I use multiple habits for bonus time but it’s a wonky workaround.

On that note there definitely need to be tasks set up as weekly or monthly targets from the get go, so we can continue recording a single streak across multiple days if all someone cares about it hitting a longer-term total target.

2. Better timer syncing. Right now if you start a timer on your phone your watch and iPad will show no progress until you pause it on the original device. If it’s still running on the original device and you start it on a second one cuz you forgot where you started it and think you forgot to start it altogether you risk erasing your progress altogether. This is a big one. Timers need to start and show in-progress time on all devices regardless of where they’re started.

3. More pages! Especially needing to add extra habits to track when I surpass my goals 12 is just not enough. Even without my “hacks” I was at 9. Why the limit? Tbh I’m not even sure pages is the best UI. Maybe just a scrolling vertical screen like on the watch?

4. The tap-and-hold UI on iPhone/iPad is not the best and it’s quite glitchy. I frequently have to do it more than once after an entry just fails to log. The circle fills up and then erases itself - animation and all! Really frustrating. The apps should all function like they do on the watch. A simple tap adds the increment. Tap and hold can open each habit to its own screen where its calendar can be modified and data viewed. Nobody needs that tiny little 2nd and 3rd screen behind the habit circle you need to enlarge first to actually use anyway.

5. Widgets and complications need help. Timers and progress are all over the place and literally never reliable. The actual time only displays 20% of the time in the widget and it’s so small even I can barely read it and I’m the weirdo who keeps her phone’s text size as small as it goes.

6. There needs to be a way to edit increments or time (for timed tasks) after the fact. If you mess up recording progress you’re basically screwed for that day. If a task has 10 increments (like my water goal) and I drink 4 glasses at once after a workout, tapping a holding 4 times to notch that up is a chore. We need to be able to bring up the habit screen and just notch up multiple increments using a dial or numerical entry. Same goes TRIPLE for timed tasks. Normal tasks worst case can be reset and manually ticked up again but if you forget to pause a timer there’s just no way to correct your day’s progress so it’s a total wash for the day. That’s kind crazy.

A way to do it would be to allow you to set a minimum and maximum number of pomodoros. So when 4 out of 16 are met, my goal completes, but I can keep going. title: Opposite color usage in widgets
body: The app itself is great so far, however: on widgets the habits you've completed are displayed in your theme color while completed are grayed out. On the apple watch (and in the app), habits you HAVEN'T completed are displayed in your theme color while completed are black & white (I'm using infograph modular). Even if you choose a custom color theme on your watch face, completed are black & white while not yet completed are grayed out. As someone with executive functioning struggles who got this app specifically for visual reasons using my watch & widgets, this virtually opposite use of visual cues between the phone and watch for complete/incomplete habits causes a lot of unnecessary friction as I have to stop and process what has been marked completed and what hasn't depending on if I'm looking at my watch or phone instead of giving clear easy information. title: Does NOT work well with multi-day, multi-part tasks.
body:
Really enjoying Streaks as a new habit tracker. Unfortunately, it doesn’t handle multi-part, multi-day tasks well. 

Example - I have three siblings. I want to call each of them once every two days. So I set up my goal for every two days, and divide my goal into three parts. 

Two things go wrong. 

First, if I do not call all three siblings on the same day, the part counter resets. This isn’t a biggie. It’s easy enough to put the info in again the next day. But it will add up to a lot of extra input over time. IMO, items in a multi-part goal over multiple days should stay filled. 

Second, Streaks means something different by “every two days” than I would. Streaks means “within two days of last completing the goal.” I mean “every two day period.”

If that sounds similar to you, here is what I mean.

Say over the next few days my goal falls Friday-Saturday, then Sunday-Monday, then Tuesday-Wednesday. On Friday, the first day of my goal, I have time to call all my siblings. Win. The next day of my goal I don’t have time, but I’ve done it already. Then we come to the next two day period (Sunday-Monday). On Sunday, I don’t have time. But on Monday I do. Then I have some time Tuesday and some Wednesday to call everyone. I have successfully completed my goal within each two day period. 

This is the same way that bill payment works. If I have a bill due every two weeks or every month, I can pay at the very beginning of one pay period and the very end of the next, with no penalty. 

Streaks, however, is programmed differently. If I complete my goal early in a two day period (Friday), it restarts the two day calendar from that point and I have to complete the next two days by Sunday. This way, I’m constantly being shortchanged if I complete my goal early. 

Imagine you have a bill due fortnightly / every two weeks. You pay on the first day of the period, but you can’t pay again till the last day of the next period. Yet each time you pay early, the company resets your pay periods so that your next payment is due in exactly two weeks, or you get a fine. Frustrating, eh? Not the way it’s supposed to be. 

As a work around, I could lengthen my goal to three or four days, but that’s not actually my goal and will result in forming a different habit. 

I’d love to see an improvement to multi-part, multi-day goals. Otherwise, I’m very happy with how Streaks is working and I look forward to using it for years.

title: The Interface and Gestures Get In The Way
body:
I wanted to like Streaks, but as time has gone on I find that the set up of the app gets in the way of actually tracking and keeping up with progress. 

It looks amazing and has a great amount of themes. The level of customization is incredible. If you’re a power user, you’re going to be very satisfied. I was very happy with the ability to customize when to get reminders and how often and with the options for how often to try to get tasks done!!! It also has very well done Apple Watch complications and app. 

Ultimately, though, I find everything takes too many taps to get to for things like history.  The UI is confusing when it comes to tracking your streaks (best, new, when you’ll break if you’re not on a daily). I don’t like the only 6 on a page set up either. I’d rather a list style with all of them showing up on the page and then maybe I could swipe to the second page for stats. 

It’s just really cumbersome to use and I felt myself trying to adapt to how the app wanted to be use, which had just grown annoying to the point of me not wanting to interface with it now looking for a more traditionally-styled app. I wish the team more continued success as it is a beautiful and very feature-rich app, just not designed for speed and utility unfortunately.
