title: A quick request for new widgets
body:
Love this app, use it all the time. Elegant and clean, highly motivating. 

I’ve been using the new widgets feature but I came across an instance that I think needs a quick fix. Right now I am tracking two tasks, one of them I do 3x / day, the other one I do 3x / week. On a day where I am doing both tasks, the weekly one fills up half the bar in the widget and the daily one fills up the other half in three increments. This is as expected. 

However, on a day where I am only doing my 3x daily task I would expect them to fill up the entire circle in three increments since I do not have my 3x weekly task scheduled on that day. (It is scheduled for Sunday, Tuesday, Thursday). However it currently is only filling up the same amount of space as on a day where I have both tasks. 

So on a Monday for example, I complete my 3x daily tasks but the progress bar on the widget only appears half full as though expecting me to complete the 3x weekly task which is not scheduled for that day. When I go into the actual app that task appears faded, yet the widget shows me that my tasks are incomplete. 

Would love to see this functionality update dynamically based on how many tasks are scheduled that day, not just all tasks regardless of how many need to be completed that day.

title: Just 12 habits?

author: Almost too good to be true

title: Very good, would be great with tweaks
body:
My main problem is that I stay up late, and I tend to log all my activity at the end of the day before I go to bed. So, regularly, I’m unable to log that I did complete a task because it’s after midnight. Things that should solve this problem: 
1. The built in “today or yesterday” prompt, which lets you catch up if you missed a day. A good add, to be sure, but only effective with tasks that are 1x/day. I should be able to catch up on a multiple times per day task, too. And, 
2. Delaying the “day starts” time in settings *should* extend the preceding day, up until the next day “starts” at the set time. Instead, at midnight you lose the ability to log the day’s streaks and then you’re stuck in limbo until the next day starts at the time you selected. That’s not very helpful IMO. 
This circumstance forces me to not only remember to do the task, but to remember to log the task as soon as it’s done. I would prefer not to have to do that, thus not a perfect app.

title: One feature is worth 5 stars by itself
body: First time ever writing an app review (I think 😅), but I’m so happy about this app I felt compelled to write. The ability to start my day at ANY time (as well as start my week on any day) is so important when building habits and consistency. Starting something—anything—new, especially if it requires the disciplined building of routines, is hardest at the beginning. Old-me inertia is easier to overcome if I can see my streaks building and the consecutive days add up. The pain-in-the-ass experience of so many productivity and habit forming apps happens when I meditate at 12:15am because I worked late. My “streak” goes back to one because it’s a new day—that is a deal breaker for me. Thanks for getting it right with a beautiful design👏🏻.

title: The simplicity is the savior

This does the job great. A quick open on the app reminds me of the various things I want keep up on, and the fact that it is there, and I can get instant feedback (complete the circle) with a calendar showing my streaks, is perfect for me.

My dailies or X times per week are pretty basic: Exercise, walk the dog, play my guitar, clean, write, read, etc., but they are essential to keeping my life active. I turned off notifications; just having the app there is motivation enough.

The key to good habits, Keep It Simple.

title: A promising app ruined by ableist ignorance.
body:
This is a pretty and well designed app. I would be perfect, but....

If you think you’re going to be able to deal with issues like executive dysfunction or establishing habits to help fight depression, you may want to look elsewhere. If you have these issues, you may find yourself wishing to include reminders and rewards for activities that others would consider mundane or automatic, like brushing your teeth or showering. However doing so will quickly bump you into the completely arbitrary 12 item limit. 

To quote their support page: 

"We understand that many users would like to create more tasks, but we encourage you to prioritize tracking the most important items to get - and keep - you on track."

Thank you for you "understanding" and your insistence that we have the same trying needs as you. We don't. We're not like you, and your refusal provide for our needs is patronizing and ableist. 

Five stars for design and concept minus four for patronizing ableism.

title: Nice UI, couple of UX oddities
body:
I really like that this app can integrate with some Health metrics and that it supports negative habits. So far, it's worth the price.

There are a couple of weird UX choices, though, in my opinion.

For some reason the app only supports up to 12 habits, and they're divided between 2 completely separate pages. I have to tap a specific button at the bottom of the screen in order to swap between them instead of being able to scroll, which is what I'd expect to be able to do.

Along the same lines, there's apparently no way to view stats (streak, # completions, percentage) for all habits together. If I tap the star icon in the bottom right of the screen, it ONLY shows stats for the (max 6) habits from the current page. This means I can have one streak count and completion rate for my first set of 6 habits, a totally different streak count for my other habits, and no way to see the overall/combined stats.

title: Game Changer
body:
I've been using this app for a good while now and it's been instrumental in my mission to attain good habits and lose ones that don't serve me. 

It's simple and easy to use and I appreciate the option to modify icons and colors so you can switch up the visuals. I say this as someone who can actually bored enough looking at the same app templates too long and then I literally don't see them anymore, like any other dusty todo list (to whoever else this applies to this will make perfect sense). 

I also really like having the ability to retroactively go back into the calendar and input details which was what lured me into going from another app to this one. I didn't want to lose track of my ongoing streaks and didn't have to with this app. Not a dealbreaker but made it all easier. 

All in all out of the other streaks-related apps and the paper method -- I find this one to be the top dog. I've gotten other people hooked on it and recommend it regularly to other people interested in employing this (very effective in my opinion) system into their regiment. 

It's allowed me to reach AND surpass yearly goals that I had much more trouble achieving before using this app as an aid. You still have to do the work, the app won't reach your goals for you. But for many I think this could be the right booster rocket to push you through.

title: Missing basic feature
body:
==TASKS==

There should be a way to set a goal for completing a task a certain number of times in a week or month not just in a day. There are some tasks where I don’t need to do a certain number of days per week, I just need to do them a certain number of times in the week. 

For example, if I want to make sure I read for 10 hours a week, it doesn’t make sense that I have to set the same time goal for each day. Instead of having to set my goal to something like “2 hours a day for 5/7 days of the week”, I’d rather just set the goal to be “10 hours for 1 week” without being forced to break it down by individual days.

The “Done” habit tracking app has this feature. I prefer this one overall, but I really miss that option from Done.

==AESTHETICS==

Also I would like a way to set the color of each task individually instead of being tied to a theme. Right now the only way to make each task a dif color is with the rainbow theme but you don’t have any control over which task is which color. 

Ideally you would also have the option to use a hexcode to specify exact colors.

But this is just visual, the actual functionality of the app is great! Just wish it would install on apple watch.

title: Nice, could’ve better
body:
Don't get me wrong.  I like the Streaks app.  Enough so that I purchased both Streaks and Streaks Workout.  But… I used them for a few months when I first purchased them, gave up when their shortcomings got too annoying, and have now, 6 months later, decided to try giving Streaks another try.  It's marginally better than the first time, but still has frustrating limitations.  I would gladly switch to another app but have not yet found a better one.  :-(
 
First, Streaks is a "Seinfelder" app - a habit tracker/trainer that is supposed to work  by inspiring you to "Don't break the chain", by making a nice big colorful mark on your calendar when you have done the wanted habit on a particular day, and a big X when you have not done so.  Inspired by Jerry Seinfeld's advice on how to develop a practice.
 
Streaks is okay as a Seinfelder app.
 
It provides a calendar for each of the 12 habits.  However, it does not provide a unified calendar, where you can see all of the habits in the same calendar box. Strange, since Streaks has nice colorful icons for each habit.  Also, Streaks does not manage to export these completion indications to Google or iCloud calendars the way similar apps do.
 
Streaks supports "negative" habits. For example, one of my negative habits is "Eating Bad Food" and "Breaking My Diet".  A negative habit starts off brightly colored and complete, and turns into an X if you admit to breaking the chain.  So far, so good.  But, there are really 3 states here:  (0) have not yet messed up, (1) messed up, X, and (3) got to end of day without messing up.   In the calendar view, these three states are a hollow circle, an X, and a filled circle, respectively.  But in the main app view state (0) have not yet messed up is confusingly indicated by the same full color icon that indicates successful completion for a positive task.
 
Streaks allows you to say that you want to do N repeats of a task per day.  E.g. I may want to stretch my injured shoulder twice a day, morning and night.  And get bonus points if I also stretch at lunch.  But Streaks does not understand "bonus points" - it stops counting after your minimum goal is reached.   Streaks does not understand that while you may want to "Keep the chain going" any day you complete more than one such task, but that you may also want to TRACK how many times you performed the task.
 
Finally: the big issue: Streaks only supports 12 tasks.  2 groups of 6.  In separate iPhone screens that you must hit a non-intuitive button to switch between.  I actually prefer the Apple Watch app for streaks, which allows me to swipe and scroll.
 
Note how I called Streaks a habit tracker/trainer?
 
Streaks is probably right in that you can really only TRAIN a small number of habits at a time.   One or two. But you can TRACK more things easily.  Note that I said "track THINGS", not "track HABITS". Indeed, TRAINing a single habit may involve TRACKing several things.
 
E.g. my sore shoulder: I want to TRAIN the stretching habit to eliminate shoulder pain.  So I would like to TRACK shoulder pain, to see if it is less on days that I have stretched.   Ditto, RMS "computeritis".
 
I.e. I want to TRACK 2 symptoms, to see if they are improved by TRAINing the habit.  And, for that matter, the see if the time of day I do my stretches correlates to the amount of pain.
 
If you say that Streaks is only about training and not tracking - well, it is that much less useful because of that limitation.   Hence my seeking a better app.
 
 
Small Stuff
 
It is good that Streaks has an Apple Watch app.  One of the main reasons I tried Streaks again.
 
Streaks supposedly does voice commands using Siri voice Shortcuts, on iPhone and Watch.  This worked for about 2 hours, then broke with "Sorry, there was a problem with the app".   Can't blame Streaks fir this, many folks report this problem with Siri voice Shortcuts.
 
Streaks' iPhone app interface is pretty, but strange, non-intuitive, and inconsistent.  E.g. it doesn't swipe between screens.  E.g. X is used for accept changes and return in some places, whereas Done is used in other places.
 
Streaks supports "Do task once every N days", etc.   But it does not support "Do task at least M times every N days".

I may want to do something at least once or twice a day, but I may want to count how many times I have done it.  I.e. count for “don’t break the chain” and count for tracking should be separate.

More and more I am making all Streaks items at least count 2 per day.  States are 0 - haven’t done anything, 1 did some, and 2 did enough, met or exceeded my goal

title: Trying to form or break a habit? This is it.
body:
I am a to-do list and productivity software connoisseur. I NEVER leave reviews. (I’m a jerk.)

This is THE BEST one out there. Why?

1) Negative habits. Most to-do lists only have affirmative goals.

2) Lightweight: Because of the health app link, while I have 12 habits set up, I only have to manually check off one affirmative habit - the rest are automatically checked off from other apps, meaning I don’t have to redundantly spend my time.

3) Meaningful metrics. I love the 7 day vs 30 day + streaks. You can see if you’re doing better this week than your past month at a glance and the extra little push of not wanting to break the streak actually influences my choices.

4) Customize-ability: For an aesthetic person it is wonderful to be able to change the look and feel.

Comments:

-The watch app is good too.

-For the negative reviews that say the interface is not intuitive. Sure maybe there’s a small learning curve but, c’mon figure it out! It’s not brain science, and once you learn it, it’s great.

-For the negative reviews that say they want more than 12. I think they made it that way for a reason: The purpose of the app is to build/break lasting habits. If you try to focus on too many, it’s likely that you’ll backslide or give up altogether. Choose 12 things you’d like to improve about yourself. Make them a habit (or break one). When you’ve mastered one, choose another.

Requests:

-It would be nice to be able to swipe between the goal sets.

-I feel like there might be a way, but if you could switch all the goals at once to calendar or stats view (maybe swiping up/down?), that’d be peachy.

Thanks Streaks!

body:

1. Allow more than 12 total tasks. How many tasks I wanna do is my business. Having a limit of 12 feels arbitrary and insane. (Am I supposed to use a different app for tasks 13 and up? It should allow at least 24.
2. Implement the swipe gesture between screens. Right now, you have to tap on the icon at the bottom of the page, which is very old fashioned. I find myself regularly trying to swipe to the next screen of tasks and getting frustrated. 
3. Would be great if there was an option to have tasks be one page that scrolls up and down, instead of only having them be discreet pages.
4. Would be nice if the task icons could be made smaller, so that there could be 3 across and maybe 4-5 down per page. (I have an iPhone XS Max, so I’d like to be able to maximize screen real estate)

author: iPhone 6+ tester

title: Very motivating
body:
I love this app. They’ve focused on quality of features rather than quantity, so while it doesn’t do a million things, it gets what it does 100% right.

What it does:
-Lets you set up a dozen or so habits you want to track (though really you should set up no more than 3-4 if you really want to stick with them)
-Choose a name, icon, and how often you want to complete each habit (daily, weekly, every Turs and Thurs, 3 times a week, etc.)
-Reminds you with notifications that you should check off completion of each habit. Checking off a habit is satisfying because it has a nice animation and a triumphant sound plays
-Lets you view your history for each habit and the total of your habits. This can be shown as a calendar, a graph or a percentage.

This app has been more than worth the money because it’s really helping me build good habits.

Some enhancements I’d like to see:
1) Ability to mark a habit as missed. If I have a habit to wake up at 7am and I’m still in bed at 8:00, I want to be able to mark the habit missed and not get notifications later in the day

2) it would be cool if there were more than one sound that plays and they were randomized. It would feel more rewarding to hear different sounds when you check off several habits in a row 

3) Another cool feature would be badges, such as “21 day streak “, “Bounced back after missing a week “, etc.

Kudos to the developers!
author: reviewer974745733

title: Great app so far, minor wishlist improvements
body:
Had the app for 2 weeks now, and really love it. It’s already helped with a few small habits and morning routines I wanted to get into. 

However, my schedule is a little different than normal — I go to bed between 2-4am nightly. So I would REALLY love an option to adjust the daily window to complete tasks, for example pushing the deadline back from midnight each night to around 2-4am, when I usuallygo to bed. I’ve consistently had to go into the app and retroactively ‘complete’ tasks from the previous day, when I’ve technically accomplished them within my own personal day. Would love it if that option could be added into the app! Or if it already is, how do I use it?

And the other thing — I’d love for just 1 more set of 6 tasks. I understand limiting the number of options so you can really focus on a few important activities, but my primary reason for getting this was to help with my small/mundane morning routine activities (such as taking vitamins, push-ups, making bed), and then I have my second set of 6 for general things I’d like to accomplish sometime throughout the day. However, I’d LOVE to be able to have 1 more set to do the same thing for a ‘night/before bed’ routine like I have for a morning routine. 

If you guys added just that 1 more set, even so it could generally be used as a ‘ Morning — Day — Night ’ list, this would be the best app I own. 

Also, the ability to swipe left or right to access the other 6 tasks instead of the button. I know that’s small haha, but after 2 weeks I still find myself trying to swipe, forgetting I have to tap the button. 

Other than that, fantastic app, really glad I got it!

title: Simple app, BIG impact!
body: Instill new habits through desire for achievement (keeping your streaks going and reminding you) versus “shoulding” yourself to do things and berating yourself if you fail. It’s more *effective* and fun for to use streaks to keep good habits (such as flossing, stretching, tracking spending, training the dog) going. I paid $4.99 for it, which is pricey for an app. But, it’s not what you pay, it’s what you *get* for what you pay. This app gave me a lot for my money and is worth it.
author: Groo_the_Wanderer

title: The Best App.
body:
Streaks has changed my life.  It's the best app I've ever gotten.  It's helped me transform so many parts of my life:
-I've reduced my youtube consumption by 75% (and haven't binge-watched since I got the app, 6 months ago)
-I sleep over an hour more a night
-I've started waking up when I set my alarms
-I drink maybe twice as much water
-I'm meditating every day
-My inbox went from 6000 emails to 0, and stayed there.
And many more.  I know what I want to be doing but sometimes I struggle to do it.  This app helps me keep doing what I want to do.  It has a power that simple promises or goals or deadlines don't—I need to keep my streaks, and I've done some crazy things to keep them.  Every time I check off a streak, from simple things to hard ones, I'm proud of myself.  I encourage you to give it a try.

If you do, here are a few quick tips:
-Start with a few, really easy streaks.  Don't set 12 things that aren't going to happen.
-Turn on "show countdown badge on app" to remind you what you still need to do
-Change the "start day at" to be a time you'll actually be asleep

One final thing I love about this app is the customization and support.  The app icon and main screen can be changed to dozens of different colors.  Initially there wasn't support for changing when the day rolled over, but I contacted the support team and it was added a few weeks later.  You can make this app your own.  Problems are quickly fixed and the experience is always improving.  I can't recommend it more.

Figuring out how to accomplish something is generally pretty intuitive but not always, and it’s hard to locate directions. A link to a FAQ or manual would be helpful.

author: 99bb

title: New features aren’t working out
body:
A recent update added the ability to set days per week, or times per day, etc.  I tried it for a while and it just doesn’t work for me. 

The original design was based on an assumption that each habit would be counted or not counted each day.

They laid a whole layer of functionality that violates that assumption on top of the original design.  The pieces don’t play well together.  It feels like they dipped a pickle in chocolate. I like pickles, and I like chocolate, but...

When each icon was either on or off every day, the simple interface was easy to interpret.  I knew at a glance exactly what the app was telling me.  Now in order to make sense of the information on the default view, I have to try to remember for each habit whether it’s daily or not, and what frequency I set it to, to understand what it’s trying to tell me and how to use it. Now, each icon is either “onasitshouldbe, shouldbeonbutisnt, didntneedtobeonbutis, or didntneedtobeonandisnt”.  Turns out that’s a whole lot more complicated than “on or off”. 

They’re going to have to redesign from the ground up if they want to make this a  complicated activity tracking app.  If they want the app to do more they need to add more visual cues.  But if they do, I probably won’t like the app anymore.  For me, the value of this app is in its simplicity.  It’s for forming good habits, not for tracking activities.

I realized, why do I need to tell this app I want to do something 3 days a week?  The old version was doing a fine job of telling me how many days a week I was doing that same thing.  Now I’m telling the app the very thing it is designed to tell me?

I’ve set all my habits back to the way they were before, and I’ll keep using the app until they jump the shark and change it into something it doesn’t need to be.

title: Doesn’t track for me
body:
Got a message from streaks that I had not completed a task. I had but went in to check. Streaks said I had completed it as well. The next day streaks showed that I no longer had a streak. This has happened more than a few times. Checked the app on my phone and watch. Both said I had finished the task yet kept getting reminders and the next day it would say I had not completed the task. Sometimes both were in agreement, sometimes not. When not I would change the one that claimed I had not completed the task. Next morning, sometimes, the streak was zeroed out. Sometimes not. 

The app also does not track my watch well. I complete three rings and Streaks sometimes says I have not and the next day my streak is over. 

To a degree I don’t care if it keeps track of the streak. Part of my life is hard to predict and missing some tasks on certain days is necessary. That said, I like to reflect and and this glitch makes that impossible. I can’t know if it was the program or me. 

I do like how the app focuses my attention and helps to form habits. Entirely worth it for just that. Not sure what else is out there but Sreaks is far better than anything I have tried. That said I will keep looking while using this app or hope this issue stops for me.

title: Good, but...
body:
I've been looking for a good habit tracker for a while. Most of them out there are either setup as a to-do task manager or a basic timer. In fact, I used to use the Things 3 app not only for my daily tasks, but also for my habits. I was really glad when I came across this, and even went far enough as to buy the bundle (streaks and workout app). The workout app needs improvement too, but that's what this review is about. 
Overall, this app seems to be working great. There's a bit of a learning curve to it, and I still don't understand why you're only allowed two pages, but overall it's pretty good. My problem with it is that sometimes when I try to delete a task (which the delete button is in a super weird place), the task pops back up numerous times in the coming days post-deletion. I delete the task, and the next day it's back and in my face. This has been happening since I've gotten the app. There's also a glitch in where when I hold down the task for completion, the icon does the little circular motion to display the button being pressed, but after the animation, it does nothing. It works usually, but sometimes it glitches out and doesn't complete the task when I tell it to.

author: Bbqscott

title: Handy, but a few things I wish for
body:
This app has already helped me make progress on some streaks, but I wish a few things:

1. More streaks (unlimited groups). I get the minimalism, but some users eventually want to build even more habits without deleting old ones, or break them into smaller achievable steps which makes 12 insufficient. In a similar vein, unlimited groups would be useful for grouping habits by interval, like daily with daily, weekly with weekly, etc, regardless of total number of habits.

2. Archiving “completed” habits. Maybe some streaks are ready to retire, but someone who cares about achieving something like a 365-day streak probably hates to just delete it like it never existed to make room for a new one. Put the archived streakes at the end out of the way. More than 6 per page would be fine.

3. Better syncing with Apple watch. I’ve noticed that if I don’t open Streaks on my phone every day - it doesn’t detect whatever I recorded on the watch app. Then I have to manually “complete” any missed days on the phone app, which isn’t the most intuitive thing in the world.

I believe if this app was updated with the few suggestions mentioned it could easily become a four or five star app.

author: ianluke

title: Rough Start
body: I bought this app based on a rave review so I have the ‘pro’ version. While it is easy to get started for basic habit tracking, I remembered reading that it could be used like a Pomodoro task master which is what I now want it for because the existing ones are either too involved ‘to do’ type apps or simplistic timers. It took quite a while to wade through how to create tasks with adequate specificity because it takes numerous passes through editing a task because all the options are not present when you first set up a habit; you create a default habit and then edit the heck out of it to get to a scheduled habit of specific length with notification reminders. It also has weird language like when it specifies the number of times a day you want to perform a habit; instead of phrasing it that way, it says “number of days” when what it means is number of times during your specified time period (day, week, month), yet the previous three options are phrased correctly. I am pretty tech savvy and it took quite a bit of playing around with the app to figure things out, even with the help section. I guess I like words more than icons (hieroglyphics as we used to call them). This app could definitely benefit by on app instructions.

Handling the advanced options is like playing with adult stuff as a child. You just poke here and there to figure out how things work. Button titles instead of ambiguous icons would help. 

On the other hand, there a few silly features like a ton of app icons you can choose from, and lots of other customizations. 

Unsure how it won an Apple Design Award!

title: Lacks critical function
body:
Lacks ability to reward for cumulative work over period of a week or two weeks when time spent each day varies day by day and week by week. 

A simple “complete the circle in X days, doesn’t matter you you do it” function would solve this and open up a lot possibility. Divide a task into pieces, complete X pieces in X days, and get rewarded along the way for each piece completed. Set alerts they way you want during that time period. 

Problem with this is the app currently wants you to assign PRECISELY the number of times per day you’re going to do something. That’s great for clock-punchers or those with regular routines. Doesn’t work for those with highly variable, unpredictable schedules. 

If there’s way to do this I’d love to know.

title: Frustrating bug
body: When it works it’s great- when it doesn’t it’s frustrating. That makes sense of course because the app has one job- one. If you complete a task but forget to mark it completed the app will fortunately allow you to mark it the next day. However IF you try to mark a task that requires multiple check ins (to be considered completed) the day after it’ll reset your streak. For example walking the dogs multiple times a day requires multiple check ins. If you forget on one day to check it in despite not missing the actual task you should be able to “mark it complete” the next day. But for what ever reason any task that involves multiple check ins will reset even if you “mark as complete for yesterday” putting you at one.

author: evrdrandosity

title: Well Designed to Develop Good Habits
body:
Streaks is well designed to help set goals for new habits and track your progress. The tasks can be customized to fit your exact goal and frequency. It only allows for six goals to be tracked so it’s not going to work for multi-task projects or a standard to-do list. Instead it’s built to help develop a few good habits at a time (e.g. walk 3 miles every Tuesday and Thursday, go to the gym three times a week, and stand up from my desk once an hour on weekdays). 

It’s very motivating to be able to mark a task complete and see the ‘streak’ number increase as I start meeting that goal more consistently. And if I’m not meeting a goal there’s no build up of incomplete to-do tasks. Intuitive reminders help remind me of the goals I’ve set and I can quickly get an overview of how many times I’ve completed a task. It’s a beautiful design with smart functionality to help me get more of what I want in my life.

title: Tricky to get into, but rewarding and customizable
body:
I bought this app after a user had stated they had achieved surprising weight goals. The biggest set back for me is procrastinating and not keeping track of my daily tasks. 

At first I was excited to set it up and test out the functionality. However, when I started using the app it was cumbersome to open each time I wanted to record a behavior. In the search/quick menu the UI buttons were small so when pressing them in vibrate mode I sometimes complete an entire multipart task instead of just the single part. There are no title separators for the icons so you had to think about the classifications and identify what groups they are yourself, this leads to searching for a while before you get through it. 

 This aside, once you get used to the UI the app is very customizable which is enjoyable. You can select multiple color schemes, icons and even the home screen app badge can be modified. The 12 tasks keep the measuring manageable, but I find that the streak is no more than a remainder. There is a sense of urgency to keep your streak going. However, I would love it if I could assign my own personal rewards for keeping a streak. This way the streak becomes more meaningful.

Great job guys, credit where it’s due. This app could change your life if you use it right. Worth the money.

This is doubly annoying when trying to view stats because you have to look at each screen individually. Graphs don’t really tell you anything. Seems designed to look nice in a preview but not really function efficiently. title: Simple and Effective.
body:
This is one of those apps that can actually make your life better. Over the past 30 days, it has helped me become more active, mindful, and disciplined.  I customize most of my streaks but I use a few preset ones too. 

For me, the key is to embrace the imperfection. I just see how high I can get my streak before breaking it. Then I try to go higher the next time. Don’t get discouraged by or try to justify a broken streak. Just beat it the next time around. 

I set the goal to pray and meditate daily. I made it 25 days until I broke my streak. No matter. I will make it at least 26 days this time. I set a goal not to use fowl language at work (with FIVE allowable slip-ups) and I haven’t made it past two days. 😂 Some streaks are going to be easier than others. I’ll get there though. 

Get this app. Use it! Beat your own records! Be better one streak at a time!!!

title: Perfect for tracking goals
body:
Love the simplicity of this tool. I use it to track my health goals (I.e.#of consecutive days without sugar, #of exercise sessions etc) and it's really helped me to stay on track. 

It's taken out a lot of my black and white thinking around my goals and I'm much happier with incremental progress. For instance, I may not be sugar free everyday, but I enjoy seeing that I'm 80% sugar free this month which is 10% better than last month. I now have real data to show me I'm moving in the direction of my goals, even if it I don't do things perfectly. 

Here are my top favorite things about it: 
1. Intuitive, uncluttered interface 
2. Ease of adding goals/targets 
3. It's rewarding to watch the wheel turn with each successful streak
4. Reminders are helpful
5. The exporting feature to track streak data over extended amounts of time.

title: Habits with a focus on simplicity
body:
Update for version 3:
This app jumped to 5 stars with its feature-rich enhancements and second screen, now allowing a dozen tracked items. I can throw my health-related goals (drink water, meditate, etc.) in one screen and my life-quality goals (e.g. Journal, Read 15 minutes, etc.) in another! And the customizations are fantastic - from the ability to change the App's springboard icon to its color-coded screens. Another very impressive update.

---

- what follows is a past review for version 2:
This app isn't suited for everyone wanting to form new habits, and for me it sits alongside "Balanced" app.

What's to like:
- It has large, simple icons in a minimalistic interface that keeps you focused on 6 core habits you want to keep track of.
- It ties into the health app so that it seamlessly checks off if you've met that health requirement for the day (e.g. Walk 5000 steps)
- It has multiple views that allow you to view you streak ratio and calendar.
- It has export functionality
- It ties to your Apple Watch

What could be improved
- You can't undo or edit historical data. If you accidentally sign off on the wrong item or - say - grab some cookies right before bed, thus invalidating your "only eat good food" goal, you can't revert.
- You can't import. This might just be the nature of having a minimalistic interface.
- You're limited to only six habits, though that might be a good thing if you're focusing on forming core habits. For people who want to monitor their day-to-day and weekly activities, Streaks will fall short. I use other programs to supplement this one and put 6 important goals in this app that I think are more necessary for my wellbeing - again, why I really like it tying to the health app.

Suggestion to users: pick six main goals that will support core habits that you want to achieve daily. Have one that's easy to achieve nearly every day but that you know you need (e.g. Eat breakfast) then three that are physical fitness oriented and two that are emotionally and mentally driven. Studies show that forming a regular health regimen acts as a catalyst to support other desirable changes in our lives. Use a different app to track all the other items if you want, but keep a minimalistic app like Streaks around to keep up with the core habits.

That said, Streaks is standalone. It does not support syncing across multiple devices, and there is no native iPad support. This type of app lends itself to being accessible everywhere you see a screen, and the lack of syncing or native iPad support is a glaring hole in its elegantly minimal feature set.

Other than this, it's a useful tool that is satisfying to use. It encourages good habits and makes me want to improve myself every time I look at it. Its widget panel and Apple Watch app make it more easily accessible, but completing the circle with device syncing would be amazing.

title: Filling circles is fun!
body:
When I looked at habit-forming apps back in 2016, I didn't even consider Streaks [$4, iOS]. This is because the app limited you to six habits you could track. No premium, in-app purchase would increase or remove that limit.

After habit building for the past year, though, I've come to agree with the app's developer: trying to concentrate on more than six habits at a time is difficult. They wisely chose this limit to help users focus.

Or maybe it's because only six rings fit comfortably on one screen. Streaks' unique interface has you tap and hold on a habit to indicate completion; a cute animation completes the ring and fills in the circle to show your progress. The app uses the same UI on its Today widget, offering a super quick method for tracking your progress.

Frankly, those two features make Streaks the easiest of these apps to use and the most fun. But I still find some downsides to using the app.

One is that the app is just willy-nilly with its reminders. You can't set what times *you* want to be reminded of your habit; instead, the app remind you whenever *it* feels like it. Another is the lack of tracking for negative habits, those which you want to break. And while you *can* track habits that require multiple completions per day, you can't log the number of completions above a set amount; for example, I can't track how many times I sent a card above my goal of two times a day. Finally, there is no way to skip a day without breaking a streak.

But if these issues don't matter to you (and, for many, they won't) or if you like the idea of auto completing habits that are Health-related, Streaks is a fine app.

title: AMAZING APP, ONE SUGGESTION
body: I usually don't give ratings but I absolutely love this app! It's great for visually being able to see how you've been holding up on your personal habits, and does a great job by holding you accountable. You're definitely going to want those streaks going on as long as possible. I've only had this app for about 4-5 days, and it's helping me to build habits out of things I've been procrastinating on doing for months. My only suggestion to enhance this app would be the ability to choose the time of day that the app resets for the next day. Basically, you have until 11:59pm each day to knock out your habits or you'll lose your streak, which forces you to mark it as done before 11:59 and just make a personal promise to yourself to get it done before bed. Sometimes you may not have time to complete everything before then. So I think being able to set the time that the habits reset for the day will be crucial, for the sake of not being forced to accomplish everything in such a rigid timeframe.

title: Needs more than 6 goals
body:
This is my favorite app for keeping track of pesky behaviors one wants to improve. It is easy to use, and very important to me, graphically very cool. An app that is graphically pleasing actually makes me want to check in and use it several times a day. And when one completes all of them in a day, they turn from white to gold. Seems like a small thing, but it is motivating.   Many of the other such apps in the store don't pass that bar with their confusing layout. 
     The one big drawback of this app is that it only allows 6 goals. I find I am more successful when I break down a goal into smaller tasks. I am working on an ongoing doctor approved daily goal of changing to a whole foods plant based diet and eliminating sugar from my diet. Also I am trying to include different types of exercise in my day: strength, cardio, balance and meditation.  
I need positive feedback throughout the day to succeed. Using one goal for "Eat Healthy Today" doesn't work for me, rather I need 5 goals, one devoted to each meal and for snacks along with a separate reminder goal of No Sweets.  With only one goal left, there isn't enough to 3 types of exercise plus daily meditation. 
     I recognize the thinking behind having just a few goals to focus on, but for those of us who need to break it down into smaller goals, 6 just isn't enough.
     It would be nice to have 12, A Daily Dozen. To keep the graphic integrity of the app, perhaps the 12 could be on two pages, 6 per page. This would solve the problem that 12 might lead to graphic clutter if all on one page. For those users for which 6 is enough, one wouldn't have to ever swipe to page 2. But for those of us who need more, a simple swipe would allow us to have the flexibility we need to be truly successful in establishing new habits.

Note 3-15-17: I originally gave 3 stars to this app, not on function or design which deserves 5 stars, but solely based on the limitation of only 6 goals. I also wrote to the app designer.  I quickly received a friendly response saying that they are already working on expanding the number of goals to a second page of 6.  For this immediate, positive feedback from the designer I have added a well-deserved 4th star.

title: Simplistic, Easy to Use, Easy to Forget
body:
I recommend this app if you're looking to create and install new, good habits into your lifestyle. There's a few things you'll need to do, and there's a couple of important ways they can improve this app.

You'll need to take a few minutes and set out customized reminders for your goals so you don't forget about them. These help, but for me they don't show up everyday or consistently. I don't know if this is a bug, but I've checked all of my notification settings. I need these to show up on my lock screen or Notification Center more liberally, perhaps even annoyingly, or else I'll forget about these habits I'm trying to work on.

One thing I recommend for new users of this app is to add it to their main home screen front and center where you'll see it multiple times each day. That'll make it a little harder to forget, even if the app doesn't send you those important reminders you wanted.

Edit: I've since followed Streaks on twitter and I wanted to add a star here because this developer is doing superb work. They actually support the app consistently, and add updates for 3D Touch and Notification Center features. I absolutely recommend this app!

title: I use Streaks every day
body:
I use Streaks every day. Yeah, I was sort of nervous about spending the few dollars to purchase this, but I knew I needed it and the app has definitely paid off! Has Streaks totally gotten me into an unfaltering daily routine of brushing my teeth and writing in Grid Diary? No. But thanks to Streaks, I'm doing it a WHOLE LOT MORE OFTEN. I love seeing my progress on their calendar and I love the satisfying feeling of pressing and holding that button to receive my check mark. Like I said, I don't always keep true to my daily habits perfectly, but I'm WAY truer to them than I was before Streaks. With Streaks, my teeth are cleaner, my soda consumption has plummeted, my journal is fuller, and my spirit is healthier. 

Get it. This is an app you won't regret buying.

body: Being newly retired I felt at a loss to know how to get personally motivated! "Streaks" gave me a way to set simple goals and to track them as they were met daily, weekly and monthly. I was able to develop self discipline around yoga, meditation, walking daily, and  time to be creative.  There are options, many choices for tasks/goals, various choices for number of times each day to complete the tasks and a way to create goals specifically for you! It has changed my perspective about how to be retired!! Give it a try! What do you have to lose!?
author: Campsitelm

title: Amazingly useful
body:
This app is really amazing.  I have been using it for a couple of months, tracking some things I want to do for myself (and for others), but don't usually do because I run out of willpower by the end of the day or just don't put my own needs ahead of other responsibilities.  Using this app changed that! I have been lifting weights, doing cardio, playing with my poor lonely cats, cleaning their water fountain, and cleaning their litter box.  I did each of these things before using this app, but it was sporadic and wholly unpredictable.  Now I (typically) do these things the number of times I defined for each task each week, and I feel great!  I've lost twenty pounds and my cats appear much happier!

At first I thought that having only six items you can track would be limiting, but as time went on I realized that I'm insanely busy, and that's why I often don't do what I intend on doing.  Keeping the number of goals small keeps it within reach.  I've typically tried to make a dozen changes all at once but have never succeeded.  I am succeeding now, and now that the gym has become habit (and even enjoyable), I'm going to remove it from Streaks and add a couple other small goals.

This is a really great app, well done, attractive, bug-free, useful, and simple. Paired with a kaizen model of small, incremental change, I consider this app the single most important tool on my phone.

title: Phenomenal App with Great Customer Service
body:
It's simple (up to 6 tasks and that's it!). It's intuitive. It's lightweight. It's beautiful. 

But then something happened in the last update. They got rid of the ability to stop health related completed notifications. Now I don't know about you, but I really cherished the silence as those notifications didn't do anything for me. If you're not familiar with the notifications, the tasks that link to the health app can trigger a notification that tells you they've been completed. But between you and me? They're useless. Why? Because you can't do anything from it. There's no action. If anything, you'll stop being active since you've completed your daily task. It's just not actionable and it's bothersome to get alert fatigue. So I emailed the developers!

They responded immediately. 

And guess what? They brought back the feature to turn them off in this update! It wasn't more than two weeks ago that I emailed them asking to bring it back that they acted upon it. They understood my qualms about alert fatigue and actionable notifications and they quickly reversed course by adding the ability to turn those notifications off. This has been the most joyful interaction I've ever had with an app developer. These guys really command an amazing ship and I wish the best for them. They're quick, smart, and great developers. And their app reflects that. 

Way to go guys! You exceeded my every expectation - so much so that I'm writing this review. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you!

I've managed to pay more attention to the ways I do and don't succeed in putting time into my own writing and reading habits, and that's a crucial first step on the way to making positive changes. title: Nice interface but limited
body:
I really love the interface and simpleness of this app. It's easy to use and keeps you focused, and is visually appealing (though that probably doesn't matter to most but it does to me). 

Unfortunately I'm going to move onto another app because they limit you on only being able to track and work on six things at a time. I get that having too many things you are working on will most likely lead to failure, but when you have lots of new habits you want to make in your life, as you start accomplishing some and want to add others it's nice to be able to still track how you are doing in the previous ones. I really wish they created space that you could swip thru to other pages and keep six per page but not limit us on our goals or what we want to track. Plus I have goals I want to track for different areas of my life and would love to be able to group them together. 

I hope they change this, but until they do it's mostly useless to me. Very sad about that!

title: Simple, Well-Executed, Excellent
body: I've tried many habits apps before this one. A list maker by nature, every activity from staying healthy to tracking homework assignments made its way onto some list app of mine. That said, I've not loved any of those more than Streaks. In it, I'm able to keep track of a *few* things that I *should* do every day while not overwhelming myself with a flood of tasks. Because of its limits on the number of trackable activities, I'm able to focus on habitually completing a small set of truly important activities each day. Its GUI is simple and flat yet perfectly sharp; complexity is not its virtue, but conciseness. I would highly recommend this app to anyone (but especially the busy at heart or the workaholic) wishing to adopt a set of daily standards unwavering for circumstances. I don't rate apps often (I haven't since I rated Civilization V on the Mac App Store), but this is a great one.

title: Simple Idea, Well Executed
body:
Some of the best iOS apps are the ones that don't try to do too much. Streaks is one of those apps. It has a nice interface, and it does what you ask it to and then gets out of your way.

I like that it's smart enough to know that, even though I've told it that I work out on every day except Monday, if I *do* happen to work out on a Monday, that gets added to my streak.

I also like the flexible way it handles notifications. I can set custom notifications for each of my items. 

And, the Watch app actually works! A rare treat, indeed. 

If you're the type of person who is motivated by that idea of checking off an item on a checklist every day, you will love this app. I'm that type of person, and my workout and creative writing routines have been recharged in the four months I've been using Streaks.

I've tried many, many apps for tracking habits and tasks, and Streaks is my absolute favorite for keeping me on track. While it's difficult to focus on all six at once, I can build momentum from one or two successful streaks and expand to the others. I'm a writer and grad student, and I would especially recommend this app to creative professionals, minimalists, and anyone who needs a little help focusing on goals.

My only disappointment is that the history goes back no further than the previous month if you've been spotty (ie not on a streak). On the one hand I guess that's a good motivation to keep a streak going; on the other, I'm losing trackable data that could help me fine-tune my approach. Hoping for more history/data analysis in future updates.

body:
This app has you put in six activities you'd like to do by day. You can customize the combination as well as change the color of the back ground. It's simple with a minimalist design. It's also easy to use. 

But the bottom line is I paid for a check list. You hold down the circles to mark off a task as completed. If you don't do it, it'll send you notifications. If you're someone serious about forming a habit and need your phone to remind you, then it may be worth the money. For me, it was nothing special. 

Be aware the app is what you make of it. It won't magically motivate you or reward you. It's just there as a reminder and keep track of what tasks you've completed. Before you drop the money, really decide if this will benefit your life. It's like a naggy spouse you can turn off, defeating the purpose.

Also it only allows you to mark a task as done or not which for habits like drinking 8 glasses of water a day is ridicules. You should be able to mark of each glass of water after you drink it instead of trying to remember how many you had at the end of the day. 

Also the reminders are set up to go off one right after the other, so if you have 6 habits you're tracking it will remind you of each one, one at a time, a couple of seconds a part. This is super annoying when your phone just starts going off at night. 

It would be great if it could also provide analytics for your habits. That way you could better identify what might be preventing you from reaching your goals. 

Ok app but far from being worth money.

title: Good not great Don't break the chain
body:
Summary - expensive for what it is - after the intrusive bold block color wears off you're left with a ui that's lacking  a big rewarding calendar or charts with bright or a well functioning watch app. The app also tells me apparently I shouldn't trying build mire than six habits with this arbitrary list limit. What if I wanted to do one thing per day? Out of luck.  

I've sent email to support and I will update my rating and review when the things I mentioned are addressed. Unfortunately right now this app is not really worth recommending.  

The long
---/
The core function is fine if very limited and on the iPhone they use tiny graphs and charts in laying the original circle icon but in the watch app you can't see the same information. In fact the watch app does virtually nothing except allow you to click done or not.   And to do that you go into the app.  Then see a display of all your items. Then tap one of them to go in. Then tap again to mark done.  Why not just allow mark done on the first screen? Also the taps register very very very poorly. Sometimes not at all and sometimes delayed three or four seconds.  Having just reloaded my Apple Watch and confirming all other apps work more speedily now this is an app specific issue. The tiny calendars is a really big error given this is a don't break the chain app.  Also No complication or glance or chart view. 

I hope to see these shortcomings rectified.  They're on the right track just missing a few things I find key.

title: Supremely good
body:
Streaks is the best way to develop a habit. The idea isn't to stuff it with to-dos or expected chores, but to choose tasks that you want to develop a habit for, and gradually, as days go by, they become part of your routine and you wouldn't need a reminder for them. And when that happens, you replace those newly formed habits with newer aspirations.

An as example, one of my tasks is "Read one New Yorker essay" set on a daily basis. The goal of this task is to get me to check my NYR subscription on a daily basis and dig into my past issues. Instead of trying to read the issues as they come out (which is incredibly difficult, and impossible for me personally) I'd read one essay per day, from any issue. Another task I have is "Read 50 pages", which I don't count my NYR essay toward. Thus, I want to develop a habit of reading (daily) through my own books, as well as catching up with relevant issues and reporting from my favorite publication. The app would nudge me every day (just once) toward that goal, reminding me to put my free time into these goals.

It's an effective way for me to be reminded of the simple pleasures or aspirations that I wish I can sustain. And it works surprisingly well.

I would like if there was a way to track things you are trying to do more than once a day like brush your teeth twice a day. It also really helps to build new habits. It takes me years to pick up new habits. Plus, since it counts how many times you've done it in a row, it totally plays on my competitive nature. title: Motivating app!
body:
Streaks is a great, easy to use app. I find that I am motivated to do things on my list--and it's not easy to motivate me! I often fall short on completing goals, but something about "circling" it off in Streaks has helped me to finish some tasks. And if you're not able to complete the task as you've set up, it actually prompts you to set a more realistic goal! 👍🏻 
As other reviewers have said, my schedule is so variable, that I really wish I could change the day of the week easier, or just say that I want to do something 3 times a week, and then choose the day myself. That's my only complaint, and why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.

title: Need more tasks
body: This is a really great reminder app. To me, it's better than a reminder because it also gives gentle encouragement to do tasks that might be bothersome or hard to remember to do every day. That's where the "streaks" feature comes in, by actually showing you your accomplishments or misses in a visual way. I love that you can chose to see it as a number or a calendar. The newest addition of the ability to choose number of times per week is really great too! For example I don't have a set schedule for exercising but I'd like to exercise 3 times per week, so now I can add that in streaks! The only thing that could make this app better is to add more tasks. Maybe the developers have a reason for only having six, but otherwise it doesn't seem hard to either allow us to flip to the next page for more or scroll down. Adding pages by category would be cool. One page for your health tasks, a page for school or work tasks, etc. or just let users name their own pages.

2.) Would like the ability to set specific days for tasks. For example, limit work tasks to only Mon-Fri.
3.) Would like to see a list view of tasks to check when I'm on my iPhone versus the circle method (which is great on the Apple Watch)

title: Really good at what it's aiming at
body:
This is a great motivational tool! It is intended to focus you on your most important goals. So you will have to make some decisions. 
First: you are limited to 6 goals. If you have more than 6 "most important goals" you will have to rethink your life. Don't blame the App. 
Second: You can pick day of the week that you want to achieve something. But if you just want to check that you've done something, let's say, 3 times a week, this is not your app. It is called Streaks for a reason: if you don't need to do it regularly, you don't need to track it here. 
Lastly, if you need to track something that you need to do more than once a day (like brushing your teeth), you can just hit complete after you did it the last time. Because that's when you've accomplished your goal. Surely, you can count to 3?
The interface is beautiful in its simplicity. I hope they don't give in to those who request more "fine tuning." And I love the somewhat hidden feature of making a completion count for the day before. Because I frequently forget to check off my goals at the end of the day. 
Thank you for a simple yet well designed App!!

Also, setting the step goal is in increments of 1,000. What if I want to set a goal of 2,500?

Anyway, with those limitations in mind, it's still a very good "don't break the chain" goal tracker.

title: Almost There!
body: I love the simplicity of this app's elegant design but it needs more robust functionality. Currently it only allows six trackable 'streaks.' I need more and strongly suspect others do, too. While limiting the number of available tasks is helpful because it encourages realistic and focused goal-setting, I suggest increasing the task limit to ten. Also, we need more customization. It's great that week can customize task reminders but I have some tasks that need to be executed more than once a day to be considered legitimate finished and therefore legitimately part of a streak (for instance I need to check my planner in the morning, afternoon, and evening). Likewise, as an example, people have to take medications more than once a day but probably don't want to create different tasks for different medications so they would want a single 'take medication' streak but with multiple customizable reminders. Ideally the task could include incremental sub-checkboxes for each increment of completion and the user could ultimately only mark the streak complete once all the checkboxes were filled (and allow the app to keep track in case they want to go back and see the details of any unfulfilled streaks, so they could see that maybe one day of the month they only checked two out of three of the checkboxes). Anyway I sincerely love the potential of this app and its beautiful design but the beauty and simplicity can be maintained even if you make the app more practical and functional.

title: More Icons Please
body:
I love the simplicity of the interface and have been using the app for a month now. It's definitely helping me be mindful of the habits I'm trying to form. Three things I would like to modify if I could:

2. A better completion satisfaction screen. I think it would be nice to have that visual reward to keep you going. Maybe a "great job, you're on a streak" message and a change of color of the screen. We all like to feel we have accomplished something. 
3. More in app suggestions I liked that after being on a streak with the amount of steps I take a day, the app asked if I wanted to increase the steps to take me to the next level. I liked that and would like to see that sort of suggestion for other tasks.

title: Wonderful and Simple! Exactly What I Needed
body: An absolutely brilliant app - not a pixel to many or too few. The only suggestion I could make would be to add configurable "days" - I normally stay up until 1 or 2AM and still want those to count towards the same day!
author: Insanj

title: A little pricy, but an excellent app.
body: Streaks has been excellent so far and while it’s not as technical as other motivation apps, the ease of use and nice app design make up for it. It would be a welcome addition to expand your streaks list to more than six, but so far, I am very happy with the app.
author: Anarkiwi

title: Start building habits
body: This little app is a tad expensive, but I'm hopeful of big things from it. The interface is incredibly easy-to-use. I, too, would like to see the ability to "fix mistakes" (undo and add a tick to a habit in the past). I recommend it, and I know you'll build habits!
author: JaysHere

title: Useless
body: This app isn't worth paying for, let alone 5 dollars, when you can't log a previous day's tasks. Particularly if you are logging something that isn't complete until the day's end (don't eat meat, etc.), this app doesn't work if your day doesn't always end before midnight. There are better apps and tools to use without spending money on this.
author: Mll5421

title: Great app, some tweaks would be nice
body: The simplicity is great. I have stayed motivated to improve what I have chosen to track since I started using the app. It would be nice to be able to edit the information from past days, however. I stayed up late working one night and before I went to bed I wanted to check off the last item of my day, but since it was 12:15 pm, the "day" had ended and I broke my streak as far as the app was concerned and I had no way to "fix" it other than starting over.
author: Plattman10

title: Sounds?
body: Great app, I actually like the 6 limit. Really wish there were sound effects though, feels unsatisfying to complete something, not even a vibration
author: Bvuygguygyigiyguyguyvuv

title: Big thumbs up.
body: Simple, delightful. Supremely functional.
author: DigDoug

title: Love this app
body: Delightful app - has helped change the way I live my life! Love it!
author: adamherscher

title: Great App!
body: This app has really done what it claims to: help me build habits. Love to see more than 6 tasks and/or ability to add tasks that need to be done multiple times per day before they can be marked as complete. Otherwise, it's become one of my staple apps!
author: It's bitadj

title: So Useful
body: I love this app. Apparently all I really needed to spice up my productive life is a little gamification. This app is simple enough that I can so easily keep track of many things I've wanted to make a daily habit of. It would be neat to see it tie in to other Health metrics, and would also benefit from a Watch component, but that would simply be icing on the cake. Get this app everyone.
author: daniel.williams

title: Simple but could be improved
body:
Great app so far. Like the simplicity.

Needs more icon options but more importantly an easier way to get through and pick them. Maybe categories vs the one big long scrolling current set up. 

Also, I would like to have more than 6 tasks to get streaks with.
author: Ryno9355

title: Love it!
body:
This app was just what I was looking for! I have so many things going on right now, so having an app remind me not to forget daily tasks is incredible. 

Just wish there was an option to go back & check of a task. I've forgotten to check it a few times, and my solution (not ideal) right now to to change my time zone to the previous day...
author: c.lobo27

title: Keeps me motivated!
body: This is a straightforward, easy to use app that helps keep your goals on track. I'm digging it!
author: Suzfabulous

title: Clean design - Great habit builder
body:
I've changed my morning routine completely with the help of this app. It makes it easy to keep track of everything, and syncs with other apps when available.  For instance, when you record your weight with MyFitnessPal, it will automatically check off "Record Weight" if you have that set as one of your items.  It has also been a great pedometer and a fun way to keep track of those daily 10,000 steps.  Again, it autofills as you walk.

I think it could priced a little lower, towards $3-4, but that's the only shortcoming.
author: Eric McCown

title: Streak
body: Please add ability to update previous days. You can break a streak just by forgetting to update before midnight. Otherwise I like this better than coach.me (formerly lift).
author: Lecky

title: Could be Better
body: Looks great, works great. But the strict construction of tasks as repetitive (i.e. can be done once a day or certain days) is a bit restrictive for my use case. Love the idea, just want the ability to add one of tasks and count 'em towards my streak!
author: rafegoldberg

title: Only Missing 2 Things
body: Great app, I love it. But it's missing the ability to manage more than six habits and the option to retroactively check off habits. Last night I didn't check the app before midnight and couldn't mark habits as completed for that previous day.
author: JustCharlie

title: Good start, basic as is
body: Remove the task limit and add countdown for tasks. Think "Drink water" with an 8 complete minimum otherwise it's not a streak. Keep up the good work. I look forward to seeing this app grow.
author: sototallycarl

title: A Great Idea
body:
I really like this app. It is simple and does what it says it does. It keeps your mind on what you say you want to do, and provides a small motivation that can be enough to get you to do those things. 

One quick suggestion, it would be really cool if there were a way to share your tasks list in a community gallery so that people could get ideas for new tasks that would be good for them. 
Thanks!
author: MaceVII

title: Needs more streaks!
body: This is a great app that encourages regular habits. It's intuitive, easy to use, and looks great! It just needs functionality to add more streaks! Why stop at six healthy habits a day when you could have 12? Definitely worth the purchase! Hopefully future updates will include more functionality.
author: JohnathanSiebert

title: Love it
body: Great, simple, intuitive app. Has helped me and several friends create/stick to streaks (habits). One recommendation to the developers: it bit would be helpful to have ability to update previous days. Example: In the present version of Streaks, if you forgot to tap a streak/goal "yesterday" it will show that you broke your streak. I assume other users will be running into this as well. Thanks!

title: Issue with Streaks Widget Not Displaying Content
body: Dear Streaks Support Team, I am experiencing an issue with the Streaks widget on my iPhone. The widget is not displaying any content, even though the app itself is working fine. I have tried the following troubleshooting steps: Ensured that the app has the necessary permissions (Motion & Fitness, Health data, etc.). Removed and re-added the widget. Restarted my iPhone. Updated Streaks to the latest version. Deleted and reinstalled the app. Despite these attempts, the widget still does not show any data. Could you please provide guidance on how to fix this issue? Thank you for your support!

author: —ES

title: Ui is not intuitive, but I respect the minimalism.
body: It’s seems to be intuitive, but the app is confusing, can’t rearrange tasks on the red board, no idea what the green board is for? When I change a task on the red board to ‘positive’ it just completes the task, I have no idea what’s going on there, seems you have to undo it, like a backwards task? Something you didn’t do? Doesn’t make sense. The icons at the bottom, cog and all are too small and non explanatory, no labels, on all time data screen the task icons at the bottom are amazingly small, no idea how it got past QA, can’t undo a task complete action if I accidentally press and hold it, gou have to erase all historical data. Pressing and holding implies that I’m going to edit the item, I think to complete a task one must click and confirm, this holding it down is not right imo. Anyway.

author: Mandzilla

title: Simple but powerful - BEST on the market!
body:
Easy to use, simple charts, quick access to record and see how you are doing. I LOVE THIS APP for its POWERFUL SIMPLICITY. The BEST on the market!!!

JUST ONE ISSUE: 
I need the ability to track more than 12 habits - 12 is just not enough when you want to track monthly tasks as well. I like tracking different things on my life wheel and breaking them down into smaller manageable tasks to track. Categories include fitness, health, social, relationships, business, mindset, creativity etc.. they all need 3-6 trackable insights. 

TO THE DEVELOPERS: 
Pls, pls, pls let us add additional groups of six things to track if we want. 24 in total would be great!! But why limit it?! Thanks!!

title: Integration!
body:
Wow, the app integration with Health is terrific. I can live my life and have this fantastic app keeping track behind the scenes. A feature I only imagined when I forgot to log certain habits in the past.

 On the watch the display is elegant and comfortable; also a “Complication”, so one can display it on the watch face. I haven’t even used this app for a complete day and I’m smitten.

Great job! Best money I’ve spent in recent memory.

HIGHLY recommended.
